title: 687. The Odyssey: Hero of the Trojan Horse (Part 1)

sentences.en: Tell me the tale of a man, Muse, who had so many roundabout ways to wander, driven off course after sacking Troy's hallowed cape.
sentences.zh: 缪斯啊，请为我讲述那一位男子的故事，他在攻陷特洛伊那神圣的城池后，被迫偏离航向，历经了无数曲折的漂泊。

sentences.en: Many of the peoples whose cities he saw, and whose ways of thinking he learned.
sentences.zh: 他见识了许多民族的城邦，也洞悉了他们的思维方式。

sentences.en: Many of the toils he suffered at tea, anguish in his heart as he struggled to safeguard his life and the homecoming of his companions.
sentences.zh: 他在海上饱受磨难，内心充满煎熬，只为竭力保全自己的性命，并护送同伴平安返乡。

sentences.en: But he did not save his companions even so, though he longed to, for their heedlessness destroyed them, theirs and nobody else's.
sentences.zh: 然而，尽管他渴望拯救同伴，却终究未能如愿，因为他们的鲁莽断送了性命，那是他们咎由自取，怨不得旁人。

sentences.en: Fools that they were, like children who devoured the sun god Hyperion's cattle.
sentences.zh: 他们真是愚不可及，竟像孩子一样吞食了太阳神许珀里翁的牛群。

sentences.en: And so he took from them the day of their homecoming.
sentences.zh: 于是，神明剥夺了他们归乡的日子。

sentences.en: Goddess, start where you will.
sentences.zh: 女神啊，请从你愿意的地方讲起吧。

sentences.en: Daughter of Zeus, share the tale with us too.
sentences.zh: 宙斯的女儿，也请与我们分享这段传奇。

sentences.en: So that was the opening of Homer's great epic, The Odyssey.
sentences.zh: 以上便是荷马史诗巨著《奥德赛》的开篇。

sentences.en: Brilliantly translated by a friend of the show, Daniel Mendelsohn.
sentences.zh: 由本节目的好友丹尼尔·门德尔松精彩翻译。

sentences.en: And there was only one person who was capable of reading that for us.
sentences.zh: 而能为我们朗读这段文字的人，只有一位。

sentences.en: And we're very grateful to the tremendous classical actor,
sentences.zh: 我们非常感谢伟大的古典派演员，

sentences.en: Russell Crowe, for reading those words.
sentences.zh: 罗素·克劳，为我们诵读了这些诗句。

sentences.en: And the reason that Russell agreed to do that for us is because the Odyssey is one of the great foundational moments,
sentences.zh: 罗素之所以答应为我们做这件事，是因为《奥德赛》是西方文化和文明中，

sentences.en: the foundational products in all Western culture and civilization.
sentences.zh: 最伟大的奠基性作品之一。

sentences.en: It ranks alongside Homer's other great poem, the Iliad, composed in the 8th or the 7th century BC.
sentences.zh: 它与荷马的另一部伟大史诗《伊利亚特》齐名，创作于公元前8世纪或7世纪。

sentences.en: And, of course, the Bible as an absolute building block of the culture that we now are so familiar with, Tom.
sentences.zh: 当然，汤姆，它和《圣经》一样，是我们如今所熟知的文化中绝对的基石。

sentences.en: So the Odyssey has given us so many other stories, hasn't it?
sentences.zh: 所以，《奥德赛》为我们衍生出了许多其他故事，不是吗？

sentences.en: You said that it's kind of foundational work of Western culture, but it's in all kinds of ways a foundational work of Western literature.
sentences.zh: 你说它是西方文化的奠基之作，但从各方面来看，它也是西方文学的奠基之作。

sentences.en: And possibly beyond that, because there are theories that perhaps the Sinbad cycle,
sentences.zh: 甚至可能不止于此，因为有理论认为，或许《辛巴达历险记》，

sentences.en: the story of Sinbad the sailor in the Arabian Nights, that perhaps that derived from the Odyssey.
sentences.zh: 也就是《一千零一夜》中辛巴达水手的故事，可能就是源自《奥德赛》。

sentences.en: Because I guess the central core idea is a pretty obvious one when you think about it,
sentences.zh: 因为我想，当你仔细思考时，其核心思想其实显而易见，

sentences.en: which is about a man far from home trying to get back to his wife, to his son, to his homeland.
sentences.zh: 那就是一个远离家乡的男人，试图回到妻子、儿子和祖国身边。

sentences.en: And in Greek, he has this kind of desperate yearning for a nostos, they called it.
sentences.zh: 在希腊语中，他有一种对“归乡”（nostos）的极度渴望，他们是这样称呼的。

sentences.en: You know, this return back home.
sentences.zh: 你知道，就是那种回到家乡的感觉。

sentences.en: And on this journey along the way, he meets with monsters and he meets with menacing alien environments and he has brushes with powers beyond the limits of mortal understanding.
sentences.zh: 在这一路上的旅程中，他遇到了怪物，遭遇了充满威胁的异域环境，并与超越凡人理解的力量有过交锋。

sentences.en: And on top of that, there are strange distortions of time and space.
sentences.zh: 不仅如此，还有时空上的诡异扭曲。

sentences.en: You have multiple narratives and you have these kind of dizzyingly subjective experiences.
sentences.zh: 你有多种叙事线索，还有那种令人眩晕的主观体验。

sentences.en: So it is, I mean, you know, people have suggested that everything that Odysseus tells us in The Odyssey may actually not be true.
sentences.zh: 所以，人们甚至提出，奥德修斯在《奥德赛》中告诉我们的一切，可能根本不是真的。

sentences.en: I mean, we don't know.
sentences.zh: 我是说，我们不得而知。

sentences.en: And that is kind of part of the fascination.
sentences.zh: 而这正是其魅力的一部分。

sentences.en: It's in one level a very simple story, a man trying to get back home.
sentences.zh: 从一个层面看，这是一个非常简单的故事：一个男人试图回家。

sentences.en: And on the other, it's kind of brilliantly sophisticated and meta.
sentences.zh: 但从另一个层面看，它又极其精妙且具有元叙事色彩。

sentences.en: You made it sound like Inception or something, you know, the Christopher Nolan film where Leonardo DiCaprio is trying to get back home to his kind of to his kids.
sentences.zh: 你把它说得像《盗梦空间》之类的电影，你知道，就是克里斯托弗·诺兰那部电影，莱昂纳多·迪卡普里奥试图回到他孩子身边。

sentences.en: And actually, that's not a coincidence because playing with time, a central character who's trying to return to something, meeting with monsters, flashbacks, flash forwards,
sentences.zh: 事实上，这并非巧合，因为玩弄时间、一个试图回归某处的核心角色、遭遇怪物、闪回、闪前，

sentences.en: a sort of dizzying whirl of events.
sentences.zh: 这一连串令人眼花缭乱的事件。

sentences.en: And you're never quite sure exactly where you are.
sentences.zh: 你永远无法确定自己到底身处何处。

sentences.en: Those are very Christopher Nolan obsessions.
sentences.zh: 这些都是克里斯托弗·诺兰非常痴迷的元素。

sentences.en: And Christopher Nolan, by an extraordinary coincidence, has made a film of The Odyssey that is coming out later this week, Tom, on the 17th of July.
sentences.zh: 而克里斯托弗·诺兰，极其巧合地，拍摄了一部《奥德赛》电影，将于本周晚些时候，即7月17日上映，汤姆。

sentences.en: There's been a lot of conversation about The Odyssey recently.
sentences.zh: 最近关于《奥德赛》的讨论非常多。

sentences.en: Quite a few controversies already thrown up before people have even seen the film.
sentences.zh: 在人们甚至还没看到电影之前，就已经引发了不少争议。

sentences.en: From the trailers and stuff, right?
sentences.zh: 是从预告片之类的东西开始的，对吧？

sentences.en: From the trailers.
sentences.zh: 是从预告片开始的。

sentences.en: And so we will be having a bonus with Daniel Mendelsohn to talk about that, and that will be out later this week.
sentences.zh: 所以我们之后会有一期与丹尼尔·门德尔松的特别节目来讨论这个话题，节目将在本周晚些时候发布。

sentences.en: So massive sense of anticipation.
sentences.zh: 所以大家充满了期待。

sentences.en: But it's not the only reason, I think, for doing The Odyssey on The Rest is History, because, to be honest, it's a story that I've been wanting to do since we began the podcaSt.
sentences.zh: 但我认为，这并不是我们在《历史的余味》中讲述《奥德赛》的唯一原因，因为老实说，这是我从节目开播以来就一直想讲的故事。

sentences.en: And I want to look at perhaps a little bit at the context.
sentences.zh: 我想稍微探讨一下它的背景。

sentences.en: So how did it come to be composed?
sentences.zh: 它是如何被创作出来的？

sentences.en: Is anything in the story true?
sentences.zh: 故事里有什么是真的吗？

sentences.en: To what degree might it be based on fact?
sentences.zh: 它在多大程度上基于事实？

sentences.en: What mirror might it hold up to the reality of the ancient Mediterranean, whether that's the time that Odysseus is supposed to have lived or the time when Homer is composing it?
sentences.zh: 它能为古代地中海的现实投射出怎样的镜像？无论是奥德修斯被认为生活的时代，还是荷马创作它的时代。

sentences.en: But also to tell the story itself,
sentences.zh: 但同时也要讲述故事本身，

sentences.en: because it is the story that first got me obsessed with Greek mythology and therefore with ancient history and therefore with history more generally.
sentences.zh: 因为它正是让我最初迷上希腊神话，进而迷上古代历史，乃至更广泛的历史的故事。

sentences.en: And so you could say that the Odyssey was the starting point for my own personal Odyssey, which has brought me to this point, Dominic, sitting here recording this episode with you.
sentences.zh: 所以你可以说，《奥德赛》是我个人奥德赛之旅的起点，它把我带到了今天，多米尼克，坐在这里和你一起录制这一集。

sentences.en: There are tens of people wiping away tears at this already.
sentences.zh: 已经有几十个人在擦眼泪了。

sentences.en: All right.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: So we're going to get into the story and we're going to try to solve some of the mysteries of the of the Odyssey.
sentences.zh: 所以我们要进入故事，尝试解开《奥德赛》中的一些谜团。

sentences.en: Now, one difference between you and Homer, I remember you saying to me when we were talking about this,
sentences.zh: 现在，你和荷马之间有一个区别，我记得我们谈论这个时你曾对我说过，

sentences.en: is that you is that you felt you could improve on Homer because you felt that Homer had made a mistake by not beginning at the beginning and proceeding chronologically.
sentences.zh: 你觉得你可以改进荷马的作品，因为你认为荷马没有从头开始并按时间顺序叙述是一个错误。

sentences.en: But you, you're going to take this different approach.
sentences.zh: 但你，你打算采取不同的方法。

sentences.en: So you're going to proceed very methodically without his haphazard approach.
sentences.zh: 所以你打算非常有条理地进行，而不是像他那样杂乱无章。

sentences.en: Am I right?
sentences.zh: 我没说错吧？

sentences.en: Well, I like to think that if that if Homer were doing it as a podcast, he would do it as I'm doing.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我喜欢认为如果荷马是在做播客，他会像我这样做。

sentences.en: I mean, if I were writing an epic poem, of course, it would be completely different.
sentences.zh: 我是说，如果我在写一部史诗，当然会完全不同。

sentences.en: But this is a podcaSt.
sentences.zh: 但这是一个播客。

sentences.en: So unlike Homer, we are going to begin at the beginning and we're going to proceed through the story chronologically, which Homer does not do.
sentences.zh: 所以与荷马不同，我们将从头开始，按时间顺序讲述故事，而荷马并没有这样做。

sentences.en: And I suspect that that's the kind of aspect of the of the epic that Christopher Nolan will be interested in.
sentences.zh: 我怀疑这正是克里斯托弗·诺兰会对这部史诗感兴趣的地方。

sentences.en: But we will see.
sentences.zh: 但我们拭目以待。

sentences.en: And to tell this story, we won't just be drawing on Homer.
sentences.zh: 为了讲述这个故事，我们不仅会参考荷马的作品。

sentences.en: However, we will occasionally be drawing on sources outside the Iliad and the Odyssey to clarify aspects of the plot that his original listeners would have taken for granted.
sentences.zh: 然而，我们偶尔会引用《伊利亚特》和《奥德赛》之外的资料，来澄清他最初的听众会视为理所当然的情节细节。

sentences.en: So let's begin right at the beginning.
sentences.zh: 那么，让我们从头开始吧。

sentences.en: And for people who don't know the Odyssey, we pick up in the final moments of the Trojan War.
sentences.zh: 对于那些不了解《奥德赛》的人，我们从特洛伊战争的最后时刻切入。

sentences.en: So Troy, the great city, the greatest city in Asia, supposedly on the banks of the Hellespont or the Dardanelles.
sentences.zh: 特洛伊，这座伟大的城市，亚洲最伟大的城市，据说是坐落在赫勒斯滂海峡或达达尼尔海峡的岸边。

sentences.en: So if you people remember the Dardanelles from our Gallipoli episode, Troy has been reduced to a smoking ruin.
sentences.zh: 如果大家还记得我们加里波利之战那一集中提到的达达尼尔海峡，特洛伊现在已经变成了一片冒烟的废墟。

sentences.en: And the people that have done this, Tom, are the Greeks.
sentences.zh: 而造成这一切的人，汤姆，是希腊人。

sentences.en: But Homer doesn't call them the Greeks, does he?
sentences.zh: 但荷马并没有称他们为希腊人，对吧？

sentences.en: No, he calls them the Achaeans.
sentences.zh: 没有，他称他们为阿开亚人。

sentences.en: So I think throughout this, these two episodes, we will be calling the Greeks the Achaeans.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为在接下来的这两集里，我们将称希腊人为阿开亚人。

sentences.en: That is the word that Homer uses.
sentences.zh: 那是荷马使用的词汇。

sentences.en: And the Achaeans and the Trojans have been fighting on the plain of Troy.
sentences.zh: 阿开亚人和特洛伊人在特洛伊平原上战斗。

sentences.en: And the Achaeans are there to seize back the kidnapped Helen, the most beautiful woman in the world who has been stolen by Paris, the prince of Troy.
sentences.zh: 阿开亚人来到这里是为了夺回被绑架的海伦，她是世界上最美丽的女人，被特洛伊王子帕里斯偷走了。

sentences.en: And the Trojans are fighting to keep her.
sentences.zh: 而特洛伊人则在为保住她而战。

sentences.en: And they've been doing this, as we say, for 10 years.
sentences.zh: 正如我们所说，他们已经这样打了10年。

sentences.en: And it looks an absolute deadlock.
sentences.zh: 看起来陷入了绝对的僵局。

sentences.en: But then, and I'm going to quote here, a bard who features in the Odyssey.
sentences.zh: 但随后，我要引用《奥德赛》中出现的一位吟游诗人。

sentences.en: And he describes how the sons of Achaean laid the city waste after pouring out of the horse.
sentences.zh: 他描述了阿开亚人的子孙在从木马中涌出后是如何将城市夷为平地的。

sentences.en: And the horse, of course, is the Trojan horse, the most successful wheeze in the whole of mythology, I would guess, in the whole history of warfare.
sentences.zh: 而这匹马，当然就是特洛伊木马，我想这可能是整个神话中，乃至整个战争史上最成功的诡计。

sentences.en: Certainly the most famous.
sentences.zh: 当然也是最著名的。

sentences.en: So famous that it inspired a disastrous project in the Gallipoli invasions, didn't it?
sentences.zh: 出名到它在加里波利入侵中激发了一个灾难性的计划，不是吗？

sentences.en: They got some ship and ran it on and it was absolute disaster.
sentences.zh: 他们找了艘船冲上去，结果是一场彻底的灾难。

sentences.en: Yeah, ran it up onto the beach and then everyone shot them.
sentences.zh: 没错，冲上海滩，然后所有人就把他们射杀了。

sentences.en: However, the original Trojan horse is not a disaster.
sentences.zh: 然而，最初的特洛伊木马并不是一场灾难。

sentences.en: It's an absolutely crunching success.
sentences.zh: 它是一次绝对震撼的成功。

sentences.en: And the person who thinks it up is the man who gives his name to the Odyssey.
sentences.zh: 而想出这个点子的人，就是《奥德赛》书名所指的那个人。

sentences.en: And this is a guy called Odysseus and he is the son of Laertes.
sentences.zh: 他叫奥德修斯，是拉尔提斯的儿子。

sentences.en: And he's the king of a very small, poor island off the west coast of Greece called Ithaca.
sentences.zh: 他是希腊西海岸一个非常贫穷的小岛——伊萨卡的国王。

sentences.en: And so relative to the other Achaean heroes at Troy, the other Greek heroes who were kings of famous golden cities like Mycenae or Sparta,
sentences.zh: 所以相对于特洛伊的其他阿开亚英雄，那些像迈锡尼或斯巴达这样著名黄金城市的国王，

sentences.en: Odysseus is very much a kind of second division king.
sentences.zh: 奥德修斯更像是一个二流国王。

sentences.en: However, he is one of the standout stars of the Trojan War.
sentences.zh: 然而，他是特洛伊战争中杰出的明星之一。

sentences.en: And this is because he has qualities that enable him to transcend the poverty of his kingdom.
sentences.zh: 这是因为他具备的品质使他能够超越其王国的贫困。

sentences.en: So he's a brilliant warrior.
sentences.zh: 他是一位出色的战士。

sentences.en: He's famous for his courage, for his prowess on the battlefield, but he's also by far the smartest of the warriors on both sides in the Trojan War.
sentences.zh: 他以勇气和战场上的英勇而闻名，但他也是特洛伊战争双方阵营中最聪明的人。

sentences.en: He's very clever.
sentences.zh: 他非常聪明。

sentences.en: He's very inventive.
sentences.zh: 他非常有创造力。

sentences.en: He's devious.
sentences.zh: 他诡计多端。

sentences.en: He's a dab hand with a trick, with a lie.
sentences.zh: 他擅长诡计和谎言。

sentences.en: And as such, he is the particular favourite of the goddess Athena, the great warrior goddess who is simultaneously the goddess of warfare,
sentences.zh: 因此，他是女神雅典娜特别宠爱的人，这位伟大的女战神既是战争女神，

sentences.en: but also the kind of the domestic sciences and everything that kind of contributes to civilisation.
sentences.zh: 也是家政科学以及所有对文明有贡献的事物的守护神。

sentences.en: And so she values intelligence for its own sake.
sentences.zh: 所以她珍视智慧本身。

sentences.en: And over the course of the Trojan War, she's always keeping an eye on him and occasionally appearing to him.
sentences.zh: 在特洛伊战争期间，她一直关注着他，并偶尔出现在他面前。

sentences.en: And she says to him, she addresses him directly.
sentences.zh: 她对他说话，直接称呼他。

sentences.en: You are by far the best of all mortal men for schemes, for your way with words, while I, more than all other gods, have a name for cunning and shrewdness.
sentences.zh: “你是所有凡人中计谋最多、口才最好的人，而我，在所有神灵中，以狡黠和精明著称。”

sentences.en: And in the Odyssey, there are a number of women who fall in love with Odysseus or who are in love with Odysseus.
sentences.zh: 在《奥德赛》中，有许多女性爱上了奥德修斯，或者说爱着奥德修斯。

sentences.en: And among those, I would rank Athena.
sentences.zh: 在她们之中，我会把雅典娜排在前面。

sentences.en: I think, you know, there is a kind of love affair there between the mortal and the goddess.
sentences.zh: 我认为，你知道，凡人与女神之间存在着一种恋情。

sentences.en: But this piece is about women falling in love with him is in the future, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 但这一段关于女性爱上他的内容是在后面才出现的，不是吗？

sentences.en: You're doing a Christopher Nolan and you're flashing forward.
sentences.zh: 你正在玩克里斯托弗·诺兰那一套，在进行闪前叙事。

sentences.en: Because, in fact, Odysseus at this point, you know, Troy is a smoking ruin.
sentences.zh: 因为事实上，此时的奥德修斯，你知道，特洛伊已是一片冒烟的废墟。

sentences.en: He has only one object in mind, and that is simply to get home as quickly as possible to his wife, Penelope, and his son, Telemachus.
sentences.zh: 他脑子里只有一个目标，那就是尽快回到他的妻子佩涅洛佩和儿子特勒马科斯身边。

sentences.en: So his son, he hasn't seen since he was a baby, basically, or a toddler.
sentences.zh: 他的儿子，他基本上从婴儿或幼儿时期就没见过面了。

sentences.en: And he's also got a dog that he's very keen on, and the dog is called Argos.
sentences.zh: 他还有一只他非常喜欢的狗，那只狗叫阿耳戈斯。

sentences.en: Yes, who Odysseus had raised him as a puppy.
sentences.zh: 是的，奥德修斯从小把它养大。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So talk to me about Penelope.
sentences.zh: 那么，跟我说说佩涅洛佩吧。

sentences.en: What's Penelope like?
sentences.zh: 佩涅洛佩是什么样的人？

sentences.en: So Penelope is obviously more important to the plot than Argos, the dog.
sentences.zh: 佩涅洛佩显然比那只叫阿耳戈斯的狗对情节更重要。

sentences.en: So Penelope is the cousin of Helen.
sentences.zh: 佩涅洛佩是海伦的表亲。

sentences.en: And Odysseus, unlike everyone else who'd gone completely mad for Helen, Odysseus had always had eyes only for Penelope.
sentences.zh: 而奥德修斯，不像其他人那样为海伦彻底疯狂，他一直只钟情于佩涅洛佩。

sentences.en: And this is because Penelope is basically very like him.
sentences.zh: 这是因为佩涅洛佩基本上和他非常像。

sentences.en: She is very clever.
sentences.zh: 她非常聪明。

sentences.en: She's very strong-minded.
sentences.zh: 她非常有主见。

sentences.en: She's absolutely suited to him.
sentences.zh: 她绝对是他的良配。

sentences.en: So she's a model of what Homer calls homophrosine, which means kind of like-mindedness.
sentences.zh: 所以她是荷马所说的“同心”（homophrosine）的典范，意思是志趣相投。

sentences.en: You have a kind of similar sensibility.
sentences.zh: 你们有一种相似的感性。

sentences.en: And Odysseus was so in love with her that prior to the departure of the Greeks for Troy, he had actually tried to get out of having to go to the expedition.
sentences.zh: 奥德修斯是如此爱她，以至于在希腊人出发前往特洛伊之前，他实际上曾试图逃避参加远征。

sentences.en: This is not in Homer,
sentences.zh: 这在荷马的作品中没有提到，

sentences.en: but people in ancient Greece listening to the Odyssey would have known that Odysseus' devotion to Penelope was such that he tried to pull this trick and get out of going to the war.
sentences.zh: 但古希腊听《奥德赛》的人都知道，奥德修斯对佩涅洛佩的深情，以至于他试图耍这个花招来逃避战争。

sentences.en: And he's the only hero of whom such a thing is recorded.
sentences.zh: 他是唯一被记载有这种行为的英雄。

sentences.en: So what had he done?
sentences.zh: 那么他做了什么？

sentences.en: When the Greek ambassadors, you know, summoning him to come to join the expedition and go to Troy with them, had arrived in Ithaca, he said,
sentences.zh: 当希腊使者来到伊萨卡，召集他参加远征并随他们一同前往特洛伊时，他说，

sentences.en: Oh, I can't come.
sentences.zh: 哦，我不能去。

sentences.en: I'm mad.
sentences.zh: 我疯了。

sentences.en: And they said, Well, in what way are you mad?
sentences.zh: 他们问，好吧，你哪里疯了？

sentences.en: And he said, Well, look at me.
sentences.zh: 他说，你看我。

sentences.en: Here I am.
sentences.zh: 我在这儿呢。

sentences.en: I've yoked a horse and an ox, and I'm ploughing a beach with salt.
sentences.zh: 我套上了一匹马和一头牛，正在用盐耕海滩。

sentences.en: Clearly, I'm absolutely mad.
sentences.zh: 显然，我彻底疯了。

sentences.en: And so most of the Greek ambassadors are persuaded by this.
sentences.zh: 于是大多数希腊使者都被说服了。

sentences.en: But one of the ambassadors is not.
sentences.zh: 但其中一位使者没有。

sentences.en: And he looks around and he sees that Telemachus' nurse is standing nearby with the baby Telemachus in her arMs.
sentences.zh: 他环顾四周，看到忒勒马科斯的保姆正站在附近，怀里抱着婴儿忒勒马科斯。

sentences.en: And so this ambassador goes over and snatches the baby and places it in front of the horse and ox as Odysseus is driving them along the beach.
sentences.zh: 于是这位使者走过去，一把抢过婴儿，放在马和牛的前面，而奥德修斯正赶着它们沿着海滩走。

sentences.en: And what's Odysseus going to do?
sentences.zh: 奥德修斯会怎么做呢？

sentences.en: He has the choice.
sentences.zh: 他面临选择。

sentences.en: He can either drive across the little baby, kill it, but not have to go to Troy or swerve and reveal that he's not actually mad.
sentences.zh: 他要么赶着牲口从婴儿身上碾过去，杀了他，但不用去特洛伊；要么转向，暴露自己其实并没有疯。

sentences.en: And so he opts to swerve and not kill his baby son.
sentences.zh: 于是他选择转向，没有杀害自己的幼子。

sentences.en: And he's rumbled.
sentences.zh: 他被识破了。

sentences.en: And so he duly has to leave for Troy.
sentences.zh: 所以他理所当然地必须启程前往特洛伊。

sentences.en: And he sets sail at the head of a fleet of 12 ships.
sentences.zh: 他率领一支由12艘船组成的船队起航了。

sentences.en: And Homer in the Iliad describes their prow's flashing crimson.
sentences.zh: 荷马在《伊利亚特》中描述他们的船头闪烁着深红色。

sentences.en: And he's there for the 10 years.
sentences.zh: 他在那里待了10年。

sentences.en: He fights heroically.
sentences.zh: 他英勇作战。

sentences.en: He comes up with the wheeze of the Trojan horse.
sentences.zh: 他想出了特洛伊木马的妙计。

sentences.en: Troy falls.
sentences.zh: 特洛伊陷落了。

sentences.en: Odysseus takes lots of loot.
sentences.zh: 奥德修斯掠夺了大量战利品。

sentences.en: He's ready to go back home.
sentences.zh: 他准备回家了。

sentences.en: Him and his 12 ships.
sentences.zh: 他和他的12艘船。

sentences.en: And so off they sail.
sentences.zh: 于是他们起航了。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: But the journey home is not quite as simple as the journey there, is it?
sentences.zh: 但回家的旅程并不像去的时候那么简单，不是吗？

sentences.en: That is putting it mildly.
sentences.zh: 这话说得还算客气了。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And this is partly because they keep getting distracted and they're distracted right from the very start.
sentences.zh: 这部分是因为他们总是分心，而且从一开始就分心了。

sentences.en: So they set off.
sentences.zh: 他们出发了。

sentences.en: The winds blow them west from Troy.
sentences.zh: 风把他们从特洛伊吹向西方。

sentences.en: They're going along the northern kind of coastline of the Aegean.
sentences.zh: 他们沿着爱琴海的北海岸航行。

sentences.en: And they arrive at a place called Ismarus.
sentences.zh: 他们到达了一个叫伊斯马罗斯的地方。

sentences.en: And there, instead of sort of putting ashore for supplies, shaking hands with the harbour master, exchanging pleasantries with the burghers of the town,
sentences.zh: 在那里，他们本该靠岸补给，与港务长握手，与镇上的市民寒暄，

sentences.en: Odysseus, by some standards, behaves very poorly.
sentences.zh: 但奥德修斯在某些标准下，表现得非常糟糕。

sentences.en: Well, he has something of the Viking about him.
sentences.zh: 嗯，他身上确实有点维京人的影子。

sentences.en: I think it's fair to say.
sentences.zh: 我觉得这么说很公道。

sentences.en: So here is Odysseus talking about what he did at Ismarus.
sentences.zh: 这是奥德修斯讲述他在伊斯马罗斯所做的事。

sentences.en: I laid waste the city and killed the men after dragging their wives from the city with a great deal of booty as well.
sentences.zh: 我洗劫了这座城市，杀死了男人，把他们的妻子从城里拖出来，还抢走了大量的战利品。

sentences.en: And it's fair to say that neither Homer nor any ancient source of which I am aware mentions what happens to these women that Odysseus and his men have kind of dragged off into slavery.
sentences.zh: 不得不说，无论是荷马还是我所知的任何古代文献，都没有提到这些被奥德修斯和他的手下拖去当奴隶的妇女后来怎么样了。

sentences.en: I mean, you know, do they die on the voyage?
sentences.zh: 我是说，她们是在航行中死去了吗？

sentences.en: I mean, are they sold?
sentences.zh: 她们被卖掉了吗？

sentences.en: I mean, we just don't know.
sentences.zh: 我们根本不知道。

sentences.en: Nothing good.
sentences.zh: 肯定没好事。

sentences.en: Nothing good, I think.
sentences.zh: 我想肯定没好事。

sentences.en: One man in Ismarus is spared.
sentences.zh: 伊斯马罗斯有一个人幸免于难。

sentences.en: And this is a guy called Maron, who is a priest of the god Apollo and his family is spared as well.
sentences.zh: 他叫马隆，是太阳神阿波罗的祭司，他的家人也幸免于难。

sentences.en: And Maron, to show his gratitude for this, gives Odysseus seven bars of gold, a silver mixing bowl and 12 amphorae of wine.
sentences.zh: 为了表示感谢，马隆送给奥德修斯七块金条、一个银制调酒碗和12坛葡萄酒。

sentences.en: And this wine is described as being sweet and undiluted, a drink for the gods.
sentences.zh: 这种酒被描述为香甜且未稀释，是神喝的饮料。

sentences.en: And we mentioned this in our episode on the history of wine.
sentences.zh: 我们在关于葡萄酒历史的那一期节目中提到过这一点。

sentences.en: It's a kind of ancient Greek premier grand cru.
sentences.zh: 这简直是古希腊的特级园佳酿。

sentences.en: It is incredibly strong.
sentences.zh: 它烈得惊人。

sentences.en: And Maron suggests to Odysseus that one portion of this wine should be mixed with 19 portions of water and that anyone who drinks it neat is obviously the most monstrous barbarian.
sentences.zh: 马隆建议奥德修斯，一份这种酒应该兑19份水，任何喝纯酒的人显然都是最野蛮的蛮族。

sentences.en: So, that is just something for listeners to bear in mind.
sentences.zh: 所以，这只是给听众提个醒。

sentences.en: And, um, Odysseus, uh, you know, he's pleased with all this.
sentences.zh: 嗯，奥德修斯，你知道，他对这一切很满意。

sentences.en: He's ready to head off.
sentences.zh: 他准备出发了。

sentences.en: But, again, this is a theme that will recur throughout the Odyssey and, indeed, these episodes.
sentences.zh: 但同样，这是一个将在《奥德赛》乃至这些剧集中反复出现的主题。

sentences.en: Um, his men, when he says, like, right, let's crack on, they've got stuck into the wine and they're also having a barbecue.
sentences.zh: 当他说“好了，我们出发吧”时，他的手下们已经喝上了酒，还在搞烧烤。

sentences.en: Hence the Russell Crowe voice for the beginning.
sentences.zh: 所以开头才用了罗素·克劳式的配音。

sentences.en: Because there's something very Australian about, about Odysseus' crew.
sentences.zh: 因为奥德修斯的船员身上有一种非常澳大利亚的感觉。

sentences.en: I mean, basically, wherever they stop, they have barbecues and start grilling meat on the beach.
sentences.zh: 基本上，无论他们停在哪里，他们都会烧烤，在海滩上烤肉。

sentences.en: And that's a terrible thing to do.
sentences.zh: 这可真是个糟糕的举动。

sentences.en: It is because, um, it enables the locals who've been beaten off to kind of rally and return to the attack with much larger numbers of men.
sentences.zh: 确实，因为这让那些被打退的当地人有机会重整旗鼓，带着更多的人回来反击。

sentences.en: And so, Odysseus and his men find themselves horribly outnumbered.
sentences.zh: 于是，奥德修斯和他的手下发现自己寡不敌众。

sentences.en: They form a shield wall.
sentences.zh: 他们组成了盾墙。

sentences.en: Um, but as the sun sets on the scene of battle, they're forced to retreat onto their ships and they manage to escape essentially by the skin of their teeth.
sentences.zh: 但在战斗场景的夕阳下，他们被迫撤退到船上，基本上是死里逃生。

sentences.en: And over 70 of his men are left dead.
sentences.zh: 他有70多名手下战死。

sentences.en: So, already the expedition is starting to leech manpower.
sentences.zh: 所以，这次远征已经开始损兵折将了。

sentences.en: However, they get away.
sentences.zh: 不过，他们还是逃脱了。

sentences.en: They sail southwards across the Aegean.
sentences.zh: 他们向南穿过爱琴海。

sentences.en: Um, they round the southernmost tip of Greece and the southernmost tip of the Peloponnese, Cape Malia.
sentences.zh: 他们绕过了希腊的最南端和伯罗奔尼撒半岛的最南端，马利亚角。

sentences.en: And now all Odysseus has to do is kind of steer around the Cape, head northwards, go around the kind of the edge of the Peloponnese.
sentences.zh: 现在奥德修斯只需要绕过海角，向北航行，沿着伯罗奔尼撒半岛的边缘走。

sentences.en: And there is Ithaca waiting for him.
sentences.zh: 伊萨卡就在那里等着他。

sentences.en: But disaster.
sentences.zh: 但灾难降临了。

sentences.en: Because as they round the Cape, a violent storm blows up.
sentences.zh: 当他们绕过海角时，一场猛烈的风暴刮了起来。

sentences.en: Terrible winds blow them and blow them and blow them.
sentences.zh: 可怕的风吹着他们，不停地吹。

sentences.en: They rage for nine days and nights.
sentences.zh: 狂风肆虐了九天九夜。

sentences.en: And when the nine days and nights of wind finally calms down, they've got no idea where they are.
sentences.zh: 当九天九夜的风终于平息时，他们根本不知道自己在哪里。

sentences.en: And on the 10th day, they see land and they moor there.
sentences.zh: 第10天，他们看到了陆地并停靠在那里。

sentences.en: And Odysseus sends a couple of scouts to go up the beach, head inland and try and work out where they are.
sentences.zh: 奥德修斯派了几个侦察兵上岸，向内陆进发，试图弄清楚他们在哪里。

sentences.en: And then he sits there and he waits for them to return.
sentences.zh: 然后他坐在那里等他们回来。

sentences.en: But they don't come back.
sentences.zh: 但他们没有回来。

sentences.en: And so finally, he thinks, well, I better go and work out what's going on here.
sentences.zh: 最后，他想，好吧，我最好去看看发生了什么事。

sentences.en: And so he leaves the ship, follows their footsteps, you know, he can trek them up the beach, goes inland and he finds them.
sentences.zh: 于是他离开船，沿着他们的足迹，他能追踪到他们上岸的痕迹，深入内陆，找到了他们。

sentences.en: And they are kind of they're half asleep.
sentences.zh: 他们半睡半醒。

sentences.en: They're all blissed out.
sentences.zh: 他们都沉浸在极乐之中。

sentences.en: They've got a kind of spaced look on their faces, smiling happily.
sentences.zh: 他们脸上带着一种恍惚的表情，幸福地微笑着。

sentences.en: And he tries to kind of rouse them, tells them, come on, we've got to get cracking.
sentences.zh: 他试图唤醒他们，告诉他们，快点，我们得出发了。

sentences.en: And they don't want to move.
sentences.zh: 但他们不想动。

sentences.en: And finally, he uses force.
sentences.zh: 最后，他动用了武力。

sentences.en: He kind of physically drags them and they start to sob.
sentences.zh: 他把他们硬拖走，他们开始啜泣。

sentences.en: They just want to stay there and chillax and, you know, have fun and be mellow and not go kind of roaring off around the world.
sentences.zh: 他们只想待在那里放松，享受生活，保持那种惬意的状态，而不是在世界上到处奔波。

sentences.en: They can't be asked to go home.
sentences.zh: 他们根本不想回家。

sentences.en: They don't want to.
sentences.zh: 他们不想走。

sentences.en: They're enjoying themselves too much where they are.
sentences.zh: 他们在那儿待得太舒服了。

sentences.en: And Odysseus realizes where they are.
sentences.zh: 奥德修斯意识到他们在哪里了。

sentences.en: They have come to the land of the lotus eaters.
sentences.zh: 他们来到了食莲人的土地。

sentences.en: And Homer explains what this means.
sentences.zh: 荷马解释了这意味着什么。

sentences.en: Now, whichever of them ate the honey sweet fruit of the lotus no longer had any desire to send word of themselves or return.
sentences.zh: 凡是吃了那种蜂蜜般香甜的莲花果实的人，就不再有任何传信或返回的念头了。

sentences.en: And so Odysseus is aware that, you know, if all his crew get out and start munching on the lotus, they will never return home.
sentences.zh: 所以奥德修斯意识到，如果他所有的船员都跑去吃莲花，他们就永远回不了家了。

sentences.en: And so he orders his fleet to leave immediately because they can't risk losing that, you know, the will for the nostos, the will for the return home.
sentences.zh: 于是他命令船队立即离开，因为他们不能冒失去那种“诺斯托斯”（nostos），即归乡意志的风险。

sentences.en: So let's just stop the story right there and ask what this is all about.
sentences.zh: 让我们在这里暂停一下，问问这到底是怎么回事。

sentences.en: So what do people think the land of the lotus eaters refers to?
sentences.zh: 人们认为食莲人的土地指的是什么？

sentences.en: Is there something in, I don't know, Bronze Age history or something that is the genesis of this idea?
sentences.zh: 在青铜时代的历史中，有什么东西是这个想法的起源吗？

sentences.en: I mean, it's a question that the Greeks themselves asked.
sentences.zh: 这是希腊人自己也问过的问题。

sentences.en: So Herodotus, the first historian,
sentences.zh: 所以希罗多德，第一位历史学家，

sentences.en: he worked out that the land of the lotus eaters must have been on the North African coast because the winds had been blowing Odysseus in that direction.
sentences.zh: 他推断食莲人的土地一定在北非海岸，因为风一直把奥德修斯吹向那个方向。

sentences.en: So this is just kind of due south of Sicily.
sentences.zh: 所以这就在西西里岛的正南方。

sentences.en: Victorian scholars thought that probably it was opium.
sentences.zh: 维多利亚时代的学者认为那可能是鸦片。

sentences.en: And I think this probably says more about the Victorians than it does about Homer because it was a great age for opium dens.
sentences.zh: 我认为这可能更多地反映了维多利亚时代的人，而不是荷马，因为那是鸦片馆盛行的时代。

sentences.en: But it's a very kind of popular idea.
sentences.zh: 但这确实是一个非常流行的想法。

sentences.en: There are other theories which I was kind of looking up for this episode.
sentences.zh: 还有其他理论，我为这期节目查了一些资料。

sentences.en: Apparently, there's a small tree called the Zizifus lotus.
sentences.zh: 显然，有一种小树叫枣莲。

sentences.en: But the problem with that is it's not narcotic.
sentences.zh: 但问题是它没有麻醉作用。

sentences.en: And there is apparently a blue lotus, which does have psychotropic properties.
sentences.zh: 据说还有一种蓝莲花，确实具有精神活性。

sentences.en: So maybe it's that.
sentences.zh: 所以也许是那个。

sentences.en: I don't know.
sentences.zh: 我不知道。

sentences.en: I'm not a specialist in the flora of North Africa.
sentences.zh: 我不是北非植物学的专家。

sentences.en: It's more likely, surely, that this is a literary symbol.
sentences.zh: 更有可能的是，这是一种文学象征。

sentences.en: The lotus eating, no?
sentences.zh: 食莲，不是吗？

sentences.en: That it's basically about losing yourself and losing sight of your goal.
sentences.zh: 这基本上是关于迷失自我和忘记目标。

sentences.en: I mean,
sentences.zh: 我是说，

sentences.en: I think it's important for the whole structure of the poem that you have to completely believe in Odysseus' desperation to get back home and that his men share in that desperation.
sentences.zh: 我认为对于整首诗的结构来说，你必须完全相信奥德修斯想要回家的那种绝望，而且他的手下也分担了这种绝望，这一点很重要。

sentences.en: And so, in a way, the best way to kind of highlight that is to show the alternative what that would mean.
sentences.zh: 所以，在某种程度上，突出这一点的最好方法就是展示另一种选择，即那意味着什么。

sentences.en: And essentially, it just means kind of chilling out and doing nothing, which might have its appeal.
sentences.zh: 本质上，它只是意味着放松和无所事事，这可能确实有吸引力。

sentences.en: But ultimately, it's seen as a danger.
sentences.zh: 但最终，这被视为一种危险。

sentences.en: And so, when Odysseus pushes off from the land of the lotus eaters, the reader or the listener can feel confident that this is a man utterly committed to getting back home.
sentences.zh: 所以，当奥德修斯离开食莲人的土地时，读者或听众可以确信，这是一个一心想要回家的人。

sentences.en: And this is very important because all kinds of obstacles, as we will see, are going to be waiting for him on his journey back.
sentences.zh: 这一点非常重要，因为正如我们将看到的，在他回家的路上，各种各样的障碍都在等着他。

sentences.en: Let's get to the next obstacle, which is the most famous obstacle of all.
sentences.zh: 让我们进入下一个障碍，这是所有障碍中最著名的一个。

sentences.en: So, they set off, don't they?
sentences.zh: 他们出发了，对吧？

sentences.en: They reach another bit of land.
sentences.zh: 他们到达了另一块陆地。

sentences.en: So, this is a little island.
sentences.zh: 这是一个小岛。

sentences.en: As far as they can tell, the island is inhabited only by wild goats.
sentences.zh: 据他们所知，岛上只住着野山羊。

sentences.en: They have another barbecue, inevitably.
sentences.zh: 他们不可避免地又搞了一次烧烤。

sentences.en: Another barbie.
sentences.zh: 又一次烧烤。

sentences.en: And they see that there's a larger island nearby.
sentences.zh: 他们看到附近有一个更大的岛屿。

sentences.en: And on this island, they can see smoke rising into the sky.
sentences.zh: 在这个岛上，他们可以看到烟雾升向天空。

sentences.en: So, that's an interesting and exciting and tantalizing sign.
sentences.zh: 这是一个有趣、令人兴奋且诱人的迹象。

sentences.en: And Odysseus, he goes off on his own, am I right, to find out what's on this island?
sentences.zh: 奥德修斯独自一人去探查岛上有什么，我没说错吧？

sentences.en: There's smoke, but there's no sign of agriculture, which is a puzzle.
sentences.zh: 有烟，但没有农业的迹象，这很令人困惑。

sentences.en: Because they would assume that a kind of a settlement people would be telling fields, but there's no sign of that.
sentences.zh: 因为他们会认为定居点的人应该会耕种田地，但那里没有这种迹象。

sentences.en: And so, Odysseus is a little bit nervous about this, not sure what that might portend.
sentences.zh: 所以奥德修斯对此有点紧张，不确定这可能预示着什么。

sentences.en: And so, he sets sail in a single ship.
sentences.zh: 于是，他乘着一艘船起航了。

sentences.en: So, he leaves the other 11 ships kind of hidden off the smaller island.
sentences.zh: 他把其他11艘船藏在较小的岛屿附近。

sentences.en: He goes off, he crosses over to the main island.
sentences.zh: 他出发了，横渡到主岛。

sentences.en: And they land, and they walk along the beach, and they see a cave.
sentences.zh: 他们登陆后，沿着海滩走，看到一个洞穴。

sentences.en: And the entrance to this cave is kind of, it's walled off with a kind of stone wall.
sentences.zh: 这个洞穴的入口被某种石墙给封住了。

sentences.en: So, he thinks, well, this is obviously signs of habitation.
sentences.zh: 于是他想，这显然是有生物居住的迹象。

sentences.en: And so, he decides to investigate.
sentences.zh: 所以他决定一探究竟。

sentences.en: And he takes his 12 bravest men with him.
sentences.zh: 他带上了他手下最勇敢的12个人。

sentences.en: And he also takes with him a goat skin filled with that delicious, very strong wine that had been given to him by Maron, the priest of Apollo.
sentences.zh: 他还带上了一羊皮袋那种美味且非常烈的美酒，那是阿波罗的祭司马隆送给他的。

sentences.en: And they go up to the cave, and they call out, and there's no answer.
sentences.zh: 他们来到洞口大声呼喊，但无人应答。

sentences.en: And so, they decide to kind of wander in and investigate.
sentences.zh: 于是他们决定走进去看看。

sentences.en: And they find that it's empty, except for lambs and for kids who are in pens.
sentences.zh: 他们发现洞里空无一人，只有羊圈里关着羔羊和幼崽。

sentences.en: And there are racks and racks of cheeses.
sentences.zh: 还有一排排的奶酪架子。

sentences.en: So, clearly, there is someone living here.
sentences.zh: 显然，这里住着人。

sentences.en: And Odysseus decides to wait for the owner of the cave to return.
sentences.zh: 奥德修斯决定等洞穴主人回来。

sentences.en: And they build a fire, and they grill some cheese.
sentences.zh: 他们生起火，烤了一些奶酪。

sentences.en: And it's like a kind of, I suppose, a kind of Mediterranean hiking holiday or something like that.
sentences.zh: 我想这就像某种地中海徒步度假之类的活动吧。

sentences.en: Again, it's this kind of Aussie-style obsession with having barbecues at inappropriate moments.
sentences.zh: 这又是一种典型的澳洲式执念，总喜欢在不合时宜的时候搞烧烤。

sentences.en: They're laid out, having this barbecue, and outside, the sun is setting.
sentences.zh: 他们正摊开身子享受烧烤，而外面太阳正在落山。

sentences.en: And towards dusk, the earth starts to shake.
sentences.zh: 黄昏时分，大地开始震动。

sentences.en: So, it's a little bit like the scene in Jurassic Park, when the glass of water on the Jeep starts to shake.
sentences.zh: 这有点像《侏罗纪公园》里那个场景，吉普车上的水杯开始震动。

sentences.en: And it's not a Tyrannosaur that appears, but a monstrous, giant human figure.
sentences.zh: 出现的不是霸王龙，而是一个巨大的怪物般的人形生物。

sentences.en: And he is driving flocks of sheep and goats ahead of him.
sentences.zh: 他赶着一群绵羊和山羊走在前面。

sentences.en: And he enters the cave.
sentences.zh: 他走进了洞穴。

sentences.en: And as he enters the cave, he blocks out the light.
sentences.zh: 当他走进洞穴时，挡住了光线。

sentences.en: As the eyes of the Achaeans adjust, they look up into his face, and they see that he has only a single eye.
sentences.zh: 当阿开亚人的眼睛适应了光线，抬头看向他的脸时，发现他只有一只眼睛。

sentences.en: So, this is a cyclops.
sentences.zh: 所以，这是一个独眼巨人。

sentences.en: And it's a cyclops by the name of Polyphemus.
sentences.zh: 这个独眼巨人名叫波吕斐摩斯。

sentences.en: And Polyphemus is of immense size and therefore strength.
sentences.zh: 波吕斐摩斯体型巨大，因此力大无穷。

sentences.en: And he picks up a giant boulder and uses it to seal the entrance.
sentences.zh: 他搬起一块巨大的圆石，用来封住洞口。

sentences.en: It would be completely impossible for Odysseus and his men to move it.
sentences.zh: 奥德修斯和他的手下根本不可能搬动它。

sentences.en: And then he looks around with his single eye, and he spots Odysseus and his men cowering at the back of the cave.
sentences.zh: 然后他用那只独眼环顾四周，发现了缩在洞穴深处的奥德修斯和他的手下。

sentences.en: And he demands to know who they are.
sentences.zh: 他质问他们是谁。

sentences.en: And just to check, do they know what he is?
sentences.zh: 顺便确认一下，他们知道他是什么吗？

sentences.en: Do they have a sense of him?
sentences.zh: 他们对他有概念吗？

sentences.en: Or is he something they've never heard of and never seen before?
sentences.zh: 还是说他是一个他们从未听说过、从未见过的事物？

sentences.en: I think the general vibe is that he's not good news.
sentences.zh: 我觉得总体感觉是，他可不是什么善茬。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: He's enormous.
sentences.zh: 他非常巨大。

sentences.en: He's fierce looking.
sentences.zh: 他看起来很凶猛。

sentences.en: He's got a single eye.
sentences.zh: 他只有一只眼睛。

sentences.en: I don't think that this is the kind of person that you probably want to run into when you've been grilling his cheese.
sentences.zh: 我觉得这绝对不是那种你想在烤人家奶酪时碰上的人。

sentences.en: But he's hopeful that perhaps he could get this guy on his side.
sentences.zh: 但他心存希望，或许能把这家伙拉拢到自己这边。

sentences.en: And so, he conquers his fear, and he steps forward, and he introduces himself.
sentences.zh: 于是他克服了恐惧，走上前去介绍自己。

sentences.en: He introduces himself as an Achaean, but he doesn't really give any more detail.
sentences.zh: 他自称是阿开亚人，但没有透露更多细节。

sentences.en: And when Polyphemus asks Odysseus, you know, well, where is your ship?
sentences.zh: 当波吕斐摩斯问奥德修斯，你知道的，你的船在哪里？

sentences.en: Odysseus lies and says that they've lost it in a storm.
sentences.zh: 奥德修斯撒谎说他们在风暴中把船弄丢了。

sentences.en: He loves a fib.
sentences.zh: 他很喜欢撒点小谎。

sentences.en: He doesn't want to give away too much because he is clearly nervous about whether Polyphemus is the kind of person you want, within whose cave you want to be stuck.
sentences.zh: 他不想透露太多，因为他显然很紧张，不知道波吕斐摩斯是不是那种你想被困在他洞里的人。

sentences.en: And when Polyphemus learns that their ship has been sunk, he reaches for two of Odysseus' men, smashes out their brains on the floor, devours them, falls asleep,
sentences.zh: 当波吕斐摩斯得知他们的船沉了之后，他抓起奥德修斯的两个手下，把他们的脑浆摔在地上，吃掉他们，然后睡着了，

sentences.en: stretched out among his flocks.
sentences.zh: 躺在他的羊群中间。

sentences.en: So, there, Dominic, is your answer.
sentences.zh: 所以，多米尼克，这就是你的答案。

sentences.en: He's not good news.
sentences.zh: 他不是什么善茬。

sentences.en: He's not the kind of person you want to be stuck in a cave with.
sentences.zh: 他不是那种你想被困在同一个洞穴里的人。

sentences.en: He's blocked them in the cave with a boulder, which is crucial.
sentences.zh: 他用一块巨石把他们堵在洞里，这很关键。

sentences.en: So, they can't just kill him because they wouldn't be able to move the boulder, right?
sentences.zh: 所以，他们不能直接杀了他，因为他们搬不动那块石头，对吧？

sentences.en: Exactly so.
sentences.zh: 正是如此。

sentences.en: So, they have no choice but to pass this completely miserable night.
sentences.zh: 所以，他们别无选择，只能熬过这个极其悲惨的夜晚。

sentences.en: And in due course, as Homer puts it, morning-born dawn touches the sky with her rosy fingertips.
sentences.zh: 正如荷马所言，晨曦女神用她玫瑰色的手指触碰天空，早晨如期而至。

sentences.en: Polyphemus wakes up, and for breakfast, he has two more of Odysseus' men.
sentences.zh: 波吕斐摩斯醒来，早餐又吃了奥德修斯的两个手下。

sentences.en: You know, he smashes them again on the kind of the side of the wall and devours them.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他再次把他们摔在墙边，然后吃掉了。

sentences.en: And then he moves the boulder, drives out his flocks, and then seals the cave up again with the boulder.
sentences.zh: 然后他移开巨石，赶出羊群，又用巨石把洞口封好。

sentences.en: So, again, you know, Odysseus and his men are stuck there.
sentences.zh: 所以，你看，奥德修斯和他的手下又被困在那里了。

sentences.en: So, you know, what are they going to do now?
sentences.zh: 那么，他们现在该怎么办呢？

sentences.en: This seems an impossible situation.
sentences.zh: 这看起来是个绝境。

sentences.en: But Odysseus, fortunately, you know, he is blindingly smart.
sentences.zh: 但幸运的是，奥德修斯聪明绝顶。

sentences.en: And so, he looks around, and he realises that there is a possible way out.
sentences.zh: 他环顾四周，意识到有一个可能的出路。

sentences.en: Because Polyphemus has got a club, and this club is enormous.
sentences.zh: 因为波吕斐摩斯有一根棍子，这根棍子非常巨大。

sentences.en: It's kind of like the size of the trunk of an enormous tree, the length and scale of the mast of a ship.
sentences.zh: 它的大小就像一棵巨树的树干，长度和规模就像一根船桅。

sentences.en: So, Odysseus gets his men to whittle this club down to a very, very sharp point.
sentences.zh: 于是奥德修斯让手下把这根棍子削得非常非常尖。

sentences.en: And then when they've done that, they conceal it under kind of sheepskins or whatever.
sentences.zh: 做完之后，他们把它藏在羊皮之类的东西下面。

sentences.en: And when Polyphemus returns that evening, he devours two more men.
sentences.zh: 当波吕斐摩斯那天晚上回来时，他又吃掉了两个人。

sentences.en: Odysseus steps forward, and he offers Polyphemus a cup of Maron's delicious, and did I mention it's very strong, wine.
sentences.zh: 奥德修斯走上前，递给波吕斐摩斯一杯马隆那美味的——我提过它非常烈吗——美酒。

sentences.en: They brought the wine with them.
sentences.zh: 他们随身带了酒。

sentences.en: Crucial.
sentences.zh: 这很关键。

sentences.en: And Polyphemus is clearly a barbarian, because he does not water it down.
sentences.zh: 波吕斐摩斯显然是个野蛮人，因为他没有兑水喝。

sentences.en: Instead, he guzzles it down neat.
sentences.zh: 相反，他直接大口干了。

sentences.en: And then when Odysseus comes forward and offers him another two cups of this wine, he guzzles that down as well.
sentences.zh: 当奥德修斯走上前再给他倒两杯酒时，他也一饮而尽。

sentences.en: And once he's had these three cups of wine, he asks Odysseus for his name.
sentences.zh: 喝了这三杯酒后，他问奥德修斯的名字。

sentences.en: And Odysseus does not give his real name.
sentences.zh: 奥德修斯没有说出真名。

sentences.en: Instead, he says, my name is Utis, which means in Greek, no one.
sentences.zh: 相反，他说，我的名字叫“无人”，在希腊语里就是“没有人”的意思。

sentences.en: Oh, so clever.
sentences.zh: 哦，太聪明了。

sentences.en: And Polyphemus says, well, you know, as a thank you for the wine, here is what I'm going to do.
sentences.zh: 波吕斐摩斯说，好吧，作为对美酒的感谢，我要这么做。

sentences.en: I will eat you laSt.
sentences.zh: 我要最后一个吃你。

sentences.en: Great giant laugh.
sentences.zh: 巨人发出大笑。

sentences.en: He then falls asleep.
sentences.zh: 然后他睡着了。

sentences.en: And as he falls asleep, he kind of belches and vomits up wine and bits of hand and bits of flesh.
sentences.zh: 在他睡着时，他打着嗝，呕吐出酒水、残肢和碎肉。

sentences.en: And it all spews out onto the floor of the cave.
sentences.zh: 这一切喷溅在洞穴的地上。

sentences.en: And Polyphemus kind of rolls over, vomits up a bit more.
sentences.zh: 波吕斐摩斯翻了个身，又吐了一些出来。

sentences.en: And then he's flat out and he's snoring.
sentences.zh: 然后他彻底瘫倒，开始打呼噜。

sentences.en: And the cave echoes to the sound of the snores.
sentences.zh: 洞穴里回荡着呼噜声。

sentences.en: And this is the chance that Odysseus has been waiting for.
sentences.zh: 这就是奥德修斯一直在等待的机会。

sentences.en: So he and his men, remember, have got this club, which they've sharpened into a spike.
sentences.zh: 所以他和他的手下，记住，他们有那根棍子，已经被削成了尖刺。

sentences.en: And they heat this giant spike in the fire.
sentences.zh: 他们把这根巨大的尖刺在火中加热。

sentences.en: And then they clamber up the body of the sleeping cyclops.
sentences.zh: 然后他们爬上熟睡的独眼巨人的身体。

sentences.en: And they aim it over his single eye.
sentences.zh: 他们对准他那只独眼。

sentences.en: Point rests on the lid.
sentences.zh: 尖端抵在眼睑上。

sentences.en: Odysseus gives the signal.
sentences.zh: 奥德修斯发出信号。

sentences.en: And then it's driven deep into the eye of the cyclops.
sentences.zh: 然后它被深深地刺入独眼巨人的眼睛里。

sentences.en: And to quote Homer, his eyelids and his brows were blistered all around by the blaSt.
sentences.zh: 引用荷马的话，他的眼睑和眉毛被灼热烧得起泡。

sentences.en: As the eyeball burned, its roots crackling in the fire.
sentences.zh: 眼球燃烧着，根部在火中发出噼啪声。

sentences.en: And understandably, Polyphemus screams and howls.
sentences.zh: 可以理解，波吕斐摩斯尖叫哀嚎。

sentences.en: He pulls the spike out of his eye and hurls it against the side of the cave and starts bellowing for help.
sentences.zh: 他把尖刺从眼睛里拔出来，扔向洞壁，开始大声呼救。

sentences.en: And there are other cyclops, you know, his neighbours.
sentences.zh: 还有其他的独眼巨人，你知道的，他的邻居们。

sentences.en: And they hear his cries and they come down and they ask him what has happened.
sentences.zh: 他们听到他的哭喊，走过来问发生了什么事。

sentences.en: And again, to quote Homer, from inside the cave, mighty Polyphemus made his reply.
sentences.zh: 再次引用荷马的话，从洞穴内，强大的波吕斐摩斯回答道。

sentences.en: Friends, no one is killing me.
sentences.zh: 朋友们，是“没有人”在杀我。

sentences.en: And so his friends answer, well, if no one is killing you, if no one has harmed you.
sentences.zh: 于是他的朋友们回答，好吧，如果“没有人”在杀你，如果“没有人”伤害你。

sentences.en: And it's clearly then just a malady sent by Zeus.
sentences.zh: 那这显然是宙斯降下的灾祸。

sentences.en: You must pray to your divine father for relief.
sentences.zh: 你必须向你的神圣父亲祈求救助。

sentences.en: And Polyphemus' divine father is Poseidon, the god of the sea.
sentences.zh: 波吕斐摩斯的神圣父亲是波塞冬，海神。

sentences.en: So a very, very powerful god indeed.
sentences.zh: 确实是一位非常非常强大的神。

sentences.en: Not good news if you want to get home by sea, right?
sentences.zh: 如果你想走海路回家，这可不是什么好消息，对吧？

sentences.en: I mean, to have Poseidon against you.
sentences.zh: 我是说，得罪了波塞冬。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 绝对是。

sentences.en: So brilliant from Odysseus.
sentences.zh: 奥德修斯真是太聪明了。

sentences.en: He's come up with the, you know, with the spike in the eye wheeze.
sentences.zh: 他想出了那个“刺瞎眼睛”的妙计。

sentences.en: And also the whole, you know, calling himself nobody means that the other cyclops think that nothing's the matter with Polyphemus.
sentences.zh: 而且自称“没有人”，让其他独眼巨人以为波吕斐摩斯没事。

sentences.en: But they're still not out of danger because what Polyphemus does now is to push back the boulder because he's got to let his flocks of sheep and goats go out.
sentences.zh: 但他们仍未脱离危险，因为波吕斐摩斯现在推开了巨石，因为他得让他的羊群出去。

sentences.en: And as they kind of start milling out through the cave entrance,
sentences.zh: 当它们开始从洞口涌出时，

sentences.en: he feels each one to make sure that Odysseus and his men aren't trying to kind of creep out hidden among the flocks.
sentences.zh: 他摸着每一只羊，确保奥德修斯和他的手下没有试图藏在羊群里溜出去。

sentences.en: But again, Odysseus is equal to this challenge.
sentences.zh: 但奥德修斯再次应对了这个挑战。

sentences.en: So what he does is he ties each of his men underneath the belly of a sheep and they all kind of manage to get out.
sentences.zh: 他把每个手下都绑在羊的肚子下面，他们就这样成功逃了出来。

sentences.en: And Polyphemus doesn't realize that they're kind of tied under the bellies of the sheep.
sentences.zh: 波吕斐摩斯没有意识到他们被绑在羊肚子下面。

sentences.en: And then he himself, there's one giant ram and he hugs onto the fleece of this giant ram and the ram trots out.
sentences.zh: 至于他自己，有一只巨大的公羊，他紧紧抱住这只公羊的羊毛，公羊小跑着出去了。

sentences.en: And Polyphemus, he strokes the ram and realizes that this is, you know, his beloved ram and feels that it's walking slowly because of the weight.
sentences.zh: 波吕斐摩斯抚摸着公羊，意识到这是他心爱的公羊，感觉到它因为负重而走得很慢。

sentences.en: But he thinks that the ram is walking slowly out of grief for his blinded master.
sentences.zh: 但他以为公羊走得慢是因为为失明的主人感到悲伤。

sentences.en: So very sad.
sentences.zh: 真是太可怜了。

sentences.en: Anyway, Odysseus and his men managed, therefore, to get out of the cave, cut themselves free from from the sheep.
sentences.zh: 总之，奥德修斯和他的手下因此成功逃出了洞穴，把自己从羊身上解开。

sentences.en: They drive the entire flock of sheep down towards their ship.
sentences.zh: 他们把整群羊赶向他们的船。

sentences.en: They load the sheep onto the boat so that, you know, they can kind of roast them later and have another barbecue.
sentences.zh: 他们把羊装上船，这样以后还能烤着吃，再来一次烧烤。

sentences.en: And then they pull out to sea.
sentences.zh: 然后他们驶向大海。

sentences.en: But Odysseus is a warrior and he wants the person he's defeated to know who has vanquished him.
sentences.zh: 但奥德修斯是个战士，他想让被他打败的人知道是谁击败了他。

sentences.en: And so he taunts the blinded cyclops from his ship as it's pulling out.
sentences.zh: 于是他在船驶离时，嘲讽了那个失明的独眼巨人。

sentences.en: And Polyphemus is so furious that he kind of gropes for the top of a mountain and pulls the summit off and hurls the rock in the direction of Odysseus.
sentences.zh: 波吕斐摩斯愤怒至极，他摸索着山顶，把山峰扯下来，朝奥德修斯的方向扔去。

sentences.en: And it lands just in front of Odysseus's ship.
sentences.zh: 它落在奥德修斯的船前。

sentences.en: And there's a great tsunami and it washes Odysseus's ship back towards the shore.
sentences.zh: 引发了巨大的海啸，把奥德修斯的船冲回了岸边。

sentences.en: And it looks like they're going to be shipwrecked on it.
sentences.zh: 看起来他们要在那儿触礁了。

sentences.en: So Odysseus takes a pole and it's kind of like a punt, you know, trying to kind of push it off the side of the river.
sentences.zh: 于是奥德修斯拿了一根杆子，就像撑船一样，试图把它从河边推开。

sentences.en: So he pushes their ship back out to sea.
sentences.zh: 他把船推回了大海。

sentences.en: He and his men row frantically.
sentences.zh: 他和手下疯狂地划桨。

sentences.en: And then again, he cannot help himself.
sentences.zh: 然后他又忍不住了。

sentences.en: And he stands on the rear of the ship and he yells taunts at Polyphemus again and fatally reveals his true identity.
sentences.zh: 他站在船尾，再次对波吕斐摩斯大声嘲讽，并致命地暴露了自己的真实身份。

sentences.en: He announces himself as Odysseus, sacker of cities, the son of Laertes, who holds his home in Ithaca.
sentences.zh: 他宣布自己是奥德修斯，劫掠城市者，拉尔提斯之子，家在伊萨卡。

sentences.en: And when Polyphemus hears this, he gives a great groan and he raises his arms and he prays to Poseidon, the god of the sea, his divine father.
sentences.zh: 当波吕斐摩斯听到这些，他发出一声长叹，举起双臂，向他的神圣父亲——海神波塞冬祈祷。

sentences.en: Hear me, Poseidon, earthshaker, you of the deep blue Maine.
sentences.zh: 听我说，波塞冬，撼地者，深蓝海洋的主宰。

sentences.en: Grant that Odysseus, sacker of cities, may never reach his home, that son of Laertes, who holds his home in Ithaca.
sentences.zh: 让奥德修斯，那个劫掠城市者，永远无法回到他的家，那个拉尔提斯之子，家在伊萨卡的人。

sentences.en: But if his fate is to see his loved ones once more and make it back home to his strong built palace and to the land of his fathers,
sentences.zh: 但如果他的命运是再次见到亲人，回到他坚固的宫殿和祖先的土地，

sentences.zh: 那就让他历经磨难，在失去所有同伴后，乘坐一艘不属于他的船，迟迟归来。

sentences.en: And may he find trouble at home.
sentences.zh: 愿他在家中也遭遇不幸。

sentences.en: That bodes very ill for Odysseus if Poseidon hears his son's prayer.
sentences.zh: 如果波塞冬听到了儿子的祈祷，这对奥德修斯来说是非常不祥的预兆。

sentences.en: And if Poseidon does hear that prayer, of course, then Odysseus's prospects of getting back to Ithaca with all of his men are hanging in the balance.
sentences.zh: 如果波塞冬真的听到了那个祈祷，那么奥德修斯带着所有手下回到伊萨卡的希望就悬于一线了。
