sentences.en: So our hero Odysseus has been swept by gales and storms far from the familiar waters of Greece and the Aegean.
sentences.zh: 我们的英雄奥德修斯被狂风暴雨卷走，远离了希腊和爱琴海那片熟悉的领域。

sentences.en: And he has ended up in a very mysterious and murky dimension.
sentences.zh: 最终他进入了一个非常神秘且阴暗的维度。

sentences.en: A place where people are off their faces on narcotic lotuses, where one-eyed monstrous giants are dashing people's brains out and having them for breakfaSt.
sentences.zh: 在那里，人们沉溺于麻醉性的莲花，独眼巨怪把人摔死当早餐吃。

sentences.en: Now to the original listeners of this story, because people would have listened to it, that have heard it rather than read it, I think.
sentences.zh: 对于这个故事最初的听众来说——因为人们是听这个故事，而不是读这个故事的，我想是这样。

sentences.en: Would they have seen these adventures?
sentences.zh: 他们会把这些当成真实的冒险吗？

sentences.en: I mean, is this the stuff of fairy tales and fantasy?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这是童话和奇幻故事吗？

sentences.en: Or did they think these things really happened?
sentences.zh: 还是他们认为这些事情真的发生过？

sentences.en: I mean, on one level, obviously, it is fantasy, but there was a sense that these islands could be located in the geography of the Mediterranean Sea.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，从某种层面上看，这显然是奇幻，但当时人们确实觉得这些岛屿可能存在于地中海的地理范围内。

sentences.en: So we've heard that Herodotus, the first great historian, he located the land of the Lotus Eaters in North Africa.
sentences.zh: 我们听说第一位伟大的历史学家希罗多德，他把食莲人的土地定位在北非。

sentences.en: And there was a tradition as well among the Greeks that the cave of Polyphemus had lain beneath Mount Etna in Sicily.
sentences.zh: 希腊人中也有一个传统，认为波吕斐摩斯的洞穴位于西西里岛的埃特纳火山之下。

sentences.en: And Etna, of course, is a volcano.
sentences.zh: 当然，埃特纳是一座火山。

sentences.en: So there is a sense of fire hidden in the mountain.
sentences.zh: 所以有一种山中藏火的感觉。

sentences.en: And the story was that the Cyclops used these fires of Etna to forge the thunderbolts that they then gave to Zeus.
sentences.zh: 故事说独眼巨人利用埃特纳的这些火来锻造雷霆，然后献给宙斯。

sentences.en: And that Polyphemus is one of the Cyclops that were working on the thunderbolts.
sentences.zh: 而波吕斐摩斯就是那些锻造雷霆的独眼巨人之一。

sentences.en: There is a brilliant theory about why one-eyed giants might have been identified with Sicily.
sentences.zh: 关于为什么独眼巨人会被与西西里岛联系在一起，有一个绝妙的理论。

sentences.en: So there's a wonderful book by a paleontologist called Adrian Meyer, who's written about what the ancients thought ancient fossils were.
sentences.zh: 古生物学家阿德里安·迈耶写过一本精彩的书，讲述了古人对古代化石的看法。

sentences.en: And she suggested that there were dwarf elephants on Sicily.
sentences.zh: 她提出西西里岛曾有过侏儒象。

sentences.en: So they'd gone extinct long before ancient Greek times, but their skulls might have been discovered.
sentences.zh: 它们在古希腊时代之前很久就灭绝了，但它们的头骨可能被发现了。

sentences.en: And because you have, you know, you have the trunk, the nasal cavity, if you look at the skull of an elephant, it does look a little bit like a kind of single eye.
sentences.zh: 因为你看，大象的头骨有象鼻和鼻腔，看起来确实有点像一只眼睛。

sentences.en: I mean, there's no proof for it, but it's a kind of, it's a wonderful idea.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这没有证据，但这真是一个绝妙的想法。

sentences.en: Is this not trying too hard to find a sort of banal, mundane explanation for what's clearly a fantastical story?
sentences.zh: 这难道不是在试图为显然是奇幻的故事寻找一种平庸、世俗的解释吗？

sentences.en: I mean, to me, it would seem like this isn't inspired by skulls of like elephants.
sentences.zh: 对我来说，这看起来并不像是受大象头骨的启发。

sentences.en: This is inspired by the fear of the unknown, the fear of the monstrous, all of that kind of stuff.
sentences.zh: 这是受对未知的恐惧、对怪物的恐惧以及诸如此类事物的启发。

sentences.en: I think that the story of these monsters lurking on strange islands, that these are anxieties that are bred of the age in which the Odyssey is being written down.
sentences.zh: 我认为这些怪物潜伏在陌生岛屿上的故事，是《奥德赛》成书那个时代所产生的焦虑。

sentences.en: And it's an age when Greek colonists are starting to settle, Sicily and the western reaches of the Mediterranean.
sentences.zh: 那是一个希腊殖民者开始在西西里岛和地中海西部边缘定居的时代。

sentences.en: And I think that Polyphemus is a kind of nightmarish vision of a barbarian who does not live by the rules of life that the Greeks associate with civilization.
sentences.zh: 我认为波吕斐摩斯是一种噩梦般的野蛮人形象，他不遵守希腊人所认知的文明生活准则。

sentences.en: So that's why Homer specifies that he drinks his wine neat.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么荷马特别提到他喝的是纯酒。

sentences.en: It's why he specifies that there's no agriculture.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么他特别提到那里没有农业。

sentences.en: These are people who, by the standards of the Greek colonists, are backward and savage and kind of frightening for that reason.
sentences.zh: 按照希腊殖民者的标准，这些人是落后、野蛮的，正因如此才令人恐惧。

sentences.en: So clearly, as you say, I mean, Polyphemus is a figure of fantasy, one of the most memorable figures in the whole history of fantasy.
sentences.zh: 所以很明显，正如你所说，波吕斐摩斯是一个奇幻人物，是整个奇幻史上最令人难忘的人物之一。

sentences.en: But he is clearly, I think, bringing to life the anxieties of adventurers who are sailing into strange seas and unsettling lands that are often very hostile.
sentences.zh: 但我认为，他显然生动地展现了那些航行在陌生海域和不安土地上的冒险者的焦虑，这些地方往往非常危险。

sentences.en: So there is a brilliant book on this by a scholar called Carol Doughty, The Raft of Odysseus.
sentences.zh: 学者卡罗尔·多蒂写过一本关于此的精彩著作《奥德修斯的木筏》。

sentences.en: And to quote from that, embedded within a familiar mythic story pattern of a time and people long ago are details and themes that belong to the contemporary world of its audience.
sentences.zh: 引用其中的话：在遥远时代和民族的熟悉神话故事模式中，嵌入了属于其受众当代世界的细节和主题。

sentences.en: And that's kind of what you would expect.
sentences.zh: 这正是你所预料的。

sentences.en: And it reminds me a bit of the way in which in the 1960s in Star Trek, if you watch it now, it's Captain Kirk going around, you know, strange planets and all of that.
sentences.zh: 这让我想起20世纪60年代的《星际迷航》，如果你现在看，那是柯克船长在各个陌生星球之间穿梭等等。

sentences.en: But so many of those episodes are plainly about anxieties and complex that are manifest in 1960s America.
sentences.zh: 但其中许多剧集显然是关于20世纪60年代美国所表现出的焦虑和情结。

sentences.en: And you would think that probably, you know, Mutatis Mutandis, the same is true of what's going on in the Odyssey, that this is fantastical,
sentences.zh: 你会认为，《奥德赛》中发生的事情可能也是如此，即它是奇幻的，

sentences.en: but it is also kind of drawing on all kinds of anxieties that reflect the character of the age in Greece.
sentences.zh: 但它也借鉴了反映希腊时代特征的各种焦虑。

sentences.en: So let's take the next adventure they have.
sentences.zh: 那么让我们看看他们的下一次冒险。

sentences.en: So this is the island of King Aeolus.
sentences.zh: 这是风神埃俄罗斯的岛屿。

sentences.en: And he is what?
sentences.zh: 他是谁？

sentences.en: He's the god of the winds.
sentences.zh: 他是风神。

sentences.en: Yeah, he's the god of the winds.
sentences.zh: 是的，他是风神。

sentences.en: And on one level, as with the Cyclops, he's plainly a fantastical figure because his island is it floats and it has ramparts made of unbreakable bronze.
sentences.zh: 在某种层面上，和独眼巨人一样，他显然是一个奇幻人物，因为他的岛屿是漂浮的，而且有坚不可摧的青铜城墙。

sentences.en: And yet at the same time, the Greeks were so confident where his island was was anchored that to this day, we call the archipelago of islands the Aeolian Islands.
sentences.zh: 然而与此同时，希腊人对他的岛屿锚地在哪里如此确信，以至于直到今天，我们仍将那片群岛称为伊奥利亚群岛。

sentences.en: Oh, yeah, of course.
sentences.zh: 哦，是的，当然。

sentences.en: It was clearly a very, very strong tradition as to where Aeolus had actually been.
sentences.zh: 关于埃俄罗斯到底在哪里，显然有一个非常非常强烈的传统。

sentences.en: I've been to the Aeolian Islands.
sentences.zh: 我去过伊奥利亚群岛。

sentences.en: They're very nice.
sentences.zh: 它们非常漂亮。

sentences.en: Lovely.
sentences.zh: 很可爱。

sentences.en: There you go.
sentences.zh: 你看，就是这样。

sentences.en: You're following in the footsteps of Odysseus.
sentences.zh: 你正在追随奥德修斯的脚步。

sentences.en: And Aeolus, unlike Polyphemus, is a very civilized man.
sentences.zh: 与波吕斐摩斯不同，埃俄罗斯是一个非常文明的人。

sentences.en: And he he's obedient to the Greek laws of what they call xenia, which is hospitality towards foreigners.
sentences.zh: 他遵守希腊人所谓的“客道”，即对外国人的好客。

sentences.en: If you meet a foreigner, the kind of mutual exchange of gifts.
sentences.zh: 如果你遇到外国人，会有那种互赠礼物的习俗。

sentences.en: The contrast with Polyphemus is very obvious and deliberate, I think.
sentences.zh: 我认为与波吕斐摩斯的对比是非常明显且刻意的。

sentences.en: And Aeolus hosts Odysseus and his men for an entire month in his kind of magnificent palace with its great bronze walls and all of that.
sentences.zh: 埃俄罗斯在那种宏伟的宫殿里招待了奥德修斯和他的手下整整一个月，宫殿有巨大的青铜墙等等。

sentences.en: And then he places all the contrary winds, the winds that would prevent Odysseus from getting back to Ithaca in a massive great bag.
sentences.zh: 然后他把所有逆风，即那些会阻止奥德修斯回到伊萨卡的风，都装进了一个巨大的袋子里。

sentences.en: And he gives this bag to Odysseus to keep in his hold.
sentences.zh: 他把这个袋子交给奥德修斯放在货舱里。

sentences.en: So you can imagine the bag kind of bulging and moving with all these winds trying to get out so that the west wind will blow him back home.
sentences.zh: 你可以想象袋子因为里面所有的风试图逃出来而鼓胀和移动，这样西风就会把他吹回家。

sentences.en: And Aeolus says, you'll be absolutely fine with this.
sentences.zh: 埃俄罗斯说，带着这个你会非常安全。

sentences.en: It's just, you know, just bear in mind the one thing, whatever you do, do not open that bag.
sentences.zh: 只是，你知道，记住一件事，无论如何，千万不要打开那个袋子。

sentences.en: And just to reiterate, whatever you do, do not open that bag.
sentences.zh: 再重申一遍，无论如何，千万不要打开那个袋子。

sentences.en: And so Odysseus, to make absolutely sure that the winds do not escape from the bag for nine days and nights, he doesn't sleep.
sentences.zh: 为了确保风在九天九夜里不会从袋子里逃出来，奥德修斯没有睡觉。

sentences.en: He sits there kind of keeping his eye on the bag.
sentences.zh: 他坐在那里盯着袋子。

sentences.en: And finally, they are so close to Ithaca that Odysseus can see smoke rising from hearth fires on the island.
sentences.zh: 最终，他们离伊萨卡如此之近，以至于奥德修斯能看到岛上炉火升起的烟雾。

sentences.en: He is so nearly there.
sentences.zh: 他离家如此之近。

sentences.en: You know, he's been awake all this time.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他一直没合眼。

sentences.en: And so fatally, he dozes off very briefly and his men, seeing him asleep, you know, they're aware that he's been watching this bag.
sentences.zh: 致命的是，他短暂地打了个盹，他的手下看到他睡着了，你知道，他们知道他一直在看守这个袋子。

sentences.en: And so they start muttering among themselves and say, well, what's in the bag?
sentences.zh: 于是他们开始私下嘀咕，说，袋子里装的是什么？

sentences.en: I mean, what's, you know, why is he so anxious about it?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，为什么他对此如此焦虑？

sentences.en: Clearly, it must be full of treasure and he's keeping it for himself and he's not sharing with us and it's not fair.
sentences.zh: 显然，里面一定装满了财宝，他想独吞，不和我们分享，这不公平。

sentences.en: So let's open up the bag and share the treasure out among ourselves before we arrive in Ithaca.
sentences.zh: 所以让我们在到达伊萨卡之前打开袋子，把财宝分了。

sentences.en: And they pull on the rope.
sentences.zh: 他们拉开了绳子。

sentences.en: They undo the bag.
sentences.zh: 他们解开了袋子。

sentences.en: The winds come screaming and howling out of the bag.
sentences.zh: 风从袋子里尖叫着呼啸而出。

sentences.en: Massive, great storMs.
sentences.zh: 巨大的风暴。

sentences.en: Odysseus is blown all the way back to the island of Iolus.
sentences.zh: 奥德修斯被吹回了伊奥利亚岛。

sentences.en: And when he goes up to Iolus and says what has happened, have you got any more winds?
sentences.zh: 当他去找伊奥利亚并说发生了什么事，你还有更多的风吗？

sentences.en: Well, basically he says, you know, will you put them in the bag again?
sentences.zh: 好吧，基本上他说，你知道，你会把它们再装进袋子里吗？

sentences.en: And Iolus says, no, get out.
sentences.zh: 伊奥利亚说，不，滚开。

sentences.en: For it's clear that you've come here as one hated by the gods.
sentences.zh: 因为很明显，你是一个被神所憎恨的人。

sentences.en: And again, you could see how if you're venturing, say, into the Western Mediterranean from Greece, a knowledge of the winds is going to be really important.
sentences.zh: 同样，你可以看出，如果你从希腊冒险进入地中海西部，了解风向将非常重要。

sentences.en: You know, getting information from local sources would be a requirement for anyone who wants to make a successful voyage.
sentences.zh: 你知道，从当地来源获取信息对于任何想要成功航行的人来说都是必须的。

sentences.en: So, again, I think you can see how that might feed into a story like this.
sentences.zh: 所以，同样，我认为你可以看出这如何融入像这样的故事中。

sentences.en: Yeah, completely.
sentences.zh: 是的，完全同意。

sentences.en: So, things have gone wrong for them.
sentences.zh: 所以，他们的情况变糟了。

sentences.en: And for the next six days, they have to row, don't they?
sentences.zh: 接下来的六天，他们不得不划船，不是吗？

sentences.en: Six days and nights.
sentences.zh: 六天六夜。

sentences.en: And they arrive in this fantastic harbour.
sentences.zh: 他们到达了这个奇妙的港口。

sentences.en: It's a perfect harbour.
sentences.zh: 这是一个完美的港口。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: High cliffs, headlands encircling it.
sentences.zh: 高耸的悬崖，岬角环绕着它。

sentences.en: And 11 of the ships go in and Odysseus' ship stays outside.
sentences.zh: 11艘船进去了，奥德修斯的船留在了外面。

sentences.en: And this is Odysseus being smart again because, Tom, what happens next?
sentences.zh: 这就是奥德修斯再次表现出聪明才智的地方，因为，汤姆，接下来发生了什么？

sentences.en: Yeah, because he can see it's a perfect harbour, but that also makes it a perfect trap.
sentences.zh: 是的，因为他能看出这是一个完美的港口，但这同时也使它成为一个完美的陷阱。

sentences.en: And Odysseus is very sensible not to have just gone ploughing in because this turns out to be the land of a people called the Lestragonians, who, again, are giant cannibals.
sentences.zh: 奥德修斯非常明智，没有直接冲进去，因为这里原来是莱斯特律戈涅斯人的领地，他们同样是巨大的食人族。

sentences.en: And there are thousands of them.
sentences.zh: 他们有成千上万的人。

sentences.en: And they all mass on the cliffs that surround this perfect harbour.
sentences.zh: 他们全都聚集在这个完美港口周围的悬崖上。

sentences.en: And again, to quote Homer, from the cliffs, they kept hurling down boulders, any one of which a man would be hard pressed to lift.
sentences.zh: 再次引用荷马的话，他们从悬崖上不断投下巨石，任何一块石头普通人都很难举起。

sentences.en: And the ships, you know, they're trapped inside this harbour and they are rapidly reduced to matchwood.
sentences.zh: 船只，你知道，被困在这个港口里，很快就被砸成了碎片。

sentences.en: And the Lestragonians then wade out into the sea and they spear Odysseus' men like their fish, like their tuna.
sentences.zh: 莱斯特律戈涅斯人随后涉水进入海中，像叉鱼一样叉奥德修斯的手下，就像叉金枪鱼一样。

sentences.en: And only Odysseus and his now solitary ship escaped the slaughter.
sentences.zh: 只有奥德修斯和他那艘孤零零的船逃过了这场屠杀。

sentences.en: So people will remember that curse that Polyphemus had laid on Odysseus, that he would return without his men.
sentences.zh: 所以人们会记得波吕斐摩斯对奥德修斯下的诅咒，他会失去所有手下独自归来。

sentences.en: Well, 11 of those ships have gone.
sentences.zh: 好吧，那11艘船已经没了。

sentences.en: And again, is there a real life equivalent to this?
sentences.zh: 同样，这在现实生活中有什么对应吗？

sentences.en: So you were talking about the Aeolian Islands and the Lotus Eaters, you know, the explanation of the Lotus Eaters.
sentences.zh: 你刚才在谈论伊奥利亚群岛和食莲人，你知道，对食莲人的解释。

sentences.en: What do historians think about the Lestragonians?
sentences.zh: 历史学家们对莱斯特律戈涅斯人怎么看？

sentences.en: The Greeks identified it again with Sicily.
sentences.zh: 希腊人再次将其与西西里岛联系起来。

sentences.en: And this is a period where they're starting to settle Sicily.
sentences.zh: 这是一个他们开始在西西里岛定居的时期。

sentences.en: And again, I think the story speaks of anxieties about murderous natives.
sentences.zh: 同样，我认为这个故事讲述了对凶残土著的焦虑。

sentences.en: And I think there's the specific twist here, which is with your ships, you see a perfect spot for a colony.
sentences.zh: 我认为这里有一个具体的转折，就是关于你的船，你看到了一个殖民的完美地点。

sentences.en: I mean, it might be a perfect spot, but that might make it all the more dangerous.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，它可能是一个完美地点，但这可能使它更加危险。

sentences.en: Because perfect spots would presumably already be settled and there would be people who would not welcome your arrival.
sentences.zh: 因为完美的地点想必已经有人定居了，而且会有不欢迎你到来的人。

sentences.en: So again, I think you can see how these stories of colonization and settlement that are coterminous with Homer's composition of the Odyssey, that this is probably what's going on,
sentences.zh: 所以同样，我认为你可以看出这些与荷马创作《奥德赛》同时代的殖民和定居故事，这可能就是当时的情况，

sentences.en: probably feeding into stories like that.
sentences.zh: 可能融入了这样的故事中。

sentences.en: Okay, so we've had a few stories that seem quite obviously to reflect anxieties about the Greek age of colonization.
sentences.zh: 好吧，我们已经讲了几个似乎很明显反映了对希腊殖民时代焦虑的故事。

sentences.en: But the next adventure is much stranger, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 但接下来的冒险要奇怪得多，不是吗？

sentences.en: And this is much more like a sort of going into some fantasy dreamscape or something.
sentences.zh: 这更像是一种进入某种奇幻梦境之类的东西。

sentences.en: Yeah, again, to kind of pursue the science fiction parallel, this is, you know, you're going through a wormhole or experiencing a singularity.
sentences.zh: 是的，再次用科幻小说来类比，这就像是你穿过了一个虫洞或经历了一个奇点。

sentences.en: You're going into a different dimension where the rules of what are normal are suspended.
sentences.zh: 你进入了一个不同的维度，那里正常的规则被暂停了。

sentences.en: However, it's not immediately obvious to Odysseus that this is what has happened.
sentences.zh: 然而，奥德修斯并没有立刻意识到这就是所发生的事情。

sentences.en: So they've made their escape from the Lestragonians.
sentences.zh: 所以他们从莱斯特律戈涅斯人那里逃了出来。

sentences.en: They keep sailing as the wind blows them and they arrive at another island.
sentences.zh: 他们随着风向继续航行，最终抵达了另一座岛屿。

sentences.en: They moor off it.
sentences.zh: 他们在岛外抛锚停泊。

sentences.en: And at first, everything seems completely normal.
sentences.zh: 起初，一切看起来都非常正常。

sentences.en: Odysseus goes on a scouting mission.
sentences.zh: 奥德修斯带人进行了一次侦察任务。

sentences.en: He runs into a stag.
sentences.zh: 他撞见了一头雄鹿。

sentences.en: He kills it.
sentences.zh: 他杀死了它。

sentences.en: He brings it back.
sentences.zh: 他把它带了回来。

sentences.en: They all have another barbecue.
sentences.zh: 他们又举行了一次烧烤聚餐。

sentences.en: The next day, Odysseus wants to go deeper into the hinterland of the island.
sentences.zh: 第二天，奥德修斯想深入岛屿腹地探查。

sentences.en: So he divides his men into two groups, one led by him, one led by a particularly brave crew member called Eurylochus and lots of cars to see which one of them,
sentences.zh: 于是他把手下分成两组，一组由他亲自带领，另一组由一位名叫欧律洛科斯的勇敢船员带领，并抽签决定，

sentences.en: which of these two groups will go and explore and which will stay and look after the ship.
sentences.zh: 看看这两组人中，哪一组去探险，哪一组留下来看守船只。

sentences.en: And the lot falls on Eurylochus to go inland and to try and scout out who or what might be on this island.
sentences.zh: 抽签结果是欧律洛科斯带队深入内陆，去探明岛上究竟有什么人或物。

sentences.en: So Eurylochus and his his scouting party head inland.
sentences.zh: 于是欧律洛科斯和他的侦察小队向内陆进发。

sentences.en: And in due course, they come to a beautiful palace with spreading lawns and gardens.
sentences.zh: 不久，他们来到了一座美丽的宫殿，那里有广阔的草坪和花园。

sentences.en: And there are wolves and lions in this garden.
sentences.zh: 花园里有狼和狮子。

sentences.en: And so, understandably, Eurylochus's men draw their swords.
sentences.zh: 理所当然地，欧律洛科斯的手下拔出了剑。

sentences.en: They're nervous of these predators.
sentences.zh: 他们对这些猛兽感到紧张。

sentences.en: But the lions and wolves seem weirdly tame.
sentences.zh: 但狮子和狼看起来却异常温顺。

sentences.en: And they fawn on Eurylochus and his men like that, you know, domestic dogs.
sentences.zh: 它们像家犬一样向欧律洛科斯和他的手下摇尾乞怜。

sentences.en: And while they're wondering about this and thinking, what on earth is going on here?
sentences.zh: 当他们对此感到疑惑，心想这到底是怎么回事时，

sentences.en: From inside the palace, they hear the beautiful voice of a woman and she's singing and she's clearly working on a loom.
sentences.zh: 他们从宫殿内听到了一个女人美妙的歌声，她显然正在织布机前忙碌。

sentences.en: And they call out to her and this woman comes to them and she opens these great gleaming doors and she invites them in.
sentences.zh: 他们呼唤她，女人便走出来，打开了那扇金碧辉煌的大门，邀请他们进去。

sentences.en: And she is fabulously gorgeous, beautifully dressed.
sentences.zh: 她美得惊人，衣着华丽。

sentences.en: Just, I mean, clearly a queen.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，她显然是一位女王。

sentences.en: And so all Eurylochus's men, except for Eurylochus himself, they walk inside.
sentences.zh: 于是，除了欧律洛科斯本人外，他所有的手下都走了进去。

sentences.en: Eurylochus, who's clearly been chosen by Odysseus because he has a quality of suspicion and intelligence that Odysseus identifies with.
sentences.zh: 欧律洛科斯之所以被奥德修斯选中，显然是因为他具备奥德修斯所认同的那种多疑和机敏的特质。

sentences.en: He stays outside.
sentences.zh: 他留在了外面。

sentences.en: He doesn't trust this woman, thinks of something a little bit sinister about her.
sentences.zh: 他不信任这个女人，觉得她身上透着一丝邪气。

sentences.en: And he's not wrong because the woman seats Eurylochus's men down on couches and then she brings them food, cheese and barley and tawny honey together with pramnian wine.
sentences.zh: 他没猜错，因为那个女人让欧律洛科斯的手下坐在长椅上，然后给他们端来了食物——奶酪、大麦、深褐色的蜂蜜，还有普拉姆尼亚酒。

sentences.en: And this food and this drink, we're told, are mixed with sinister drugs.
sentences.zh: 我们被告知，这些食物和饮料中混入了邪恶的药物。

sentences.en: And Eurylochus's men eat and drink their fill.
sentences.zh: 欧律洛科斯的手下大快朵颐，吃喝个够。

sentences.en: And then once they have gorged themselves, the woman walks around the dining area and she taps them with a wand and immediately they start turning into pigs.
sentences.zh: 当他们酒足饭饱后，女人在餐厅里走动，用魔杖轻触他们，他们立刻开始变成猪。

sentences.en: Their heads, their grunts, their bristles, their bodies, although their minds were as sound as they'd always been.
sentences.zh: 他们的头、叫声、鬃毛和身体都变了，但他们的心智却依然如故。

sentences.en: So they are humans trapped in the bodies of a pig.
sentences.zh: 所以他们是困在猪躯体里的人类。

sentences.en: And Eurylochus has watched all of this and he manages to get away and he runs back to Odysseus, reports it to Odysseus.
sentences.zh: 欧律洛科斯目睹了这一切，他设法逃脱并跑回奥德修斯那里，向他报告了情况。

sentences.en: And from this point on, the story becomes even stranger.
sentences.zh: 从这一点开始，故事变得更加离奇了。

sentences.en: So Odysseus is determined to redeem his men from the spell.
sentences.zh: 奥德修斯决心从咒语中解救他的手下。

sentences.en: You know, aside from anything else, he needs them.
sentences.zh: 毕竟，他还需要他们。

sentences.en: He won't be able to kind of row the ship without them.
sentences.zh: 没有他们，他根本无法划船。

sentences.en: So he sets off to confront this woman who is patently a sorceress.
sentences.zh: 于是他出发去对抗这个显然是女巫的女人。

sentences.en: And on his way, he meets for the first time in the course of his wanderings, a bona fide Olympian, one of the top 12 gods on Mount Olympus.
sentences.zh: 在途中，他在流浪过程中第一次遇见了一位真正的奥林匹斯神，也就是奥林匹斯山上十二主神之一。

sentences.en: And this is Hermes, the messenger of the gods.
sentences.zh: 这就是众神的信使赫尔墨斯。

sentences.en: So has clearly been sent by someone, we presume Athena, to help him out.
sentences.zh: 他显然是受某人——我们推测是雅典娜——之托来帮助奥德修斯的。

sentences.en: And Hermes gives Odysseus an awesome drug of his own.
sentences.zh: 赫尔墨斯给了奥德修斯一种神奇的药物。

sentences.en: And this is a black rooted herb with a white flower called the moly.
sentences.zh: 这是一种黑根白花的草药，名叫“莫吕”。

sentences.en: And armed with the moly, and it's unclear exactly what the moly might be based on.
sentences.zh: 有了莫吕在手——虽然不清楚莫吕到底是以什么为原型——

sentences.en: But anyway, it's very powerful, has great magic.
sentences.zh: 总之，它非常强大，具有伟大的魔力。

sentences.en: Odysseus proves immune to the sorceress's spells.
sentences.zh: 奥德修斯证明了自己对女巫的咒语免疫。

sentences.en: And this is despite the fact that we discover this sorceress is herself a goddess.
sentences.zh: 尽管我们发现这个女巫本身也是一位女神。

sentences.en: She is a daughter of the sun and her name is Circe of the Beautiful Braids.
sentences.zh: 她是太阳之女，名叫“美发喀耳刻”。

sentences.en: And at sword point, Odysseus forces Circe to submit and Circe submits and then invites Odysseus to bed.
sentences.zh: 在剑锋之下，奥德修斯强迫喀耳刻屈服，喀耳刻屈服了，随后邀请奥德修斯共赴云雨。

sentences.en: And Odysseus says, no way, unless you could bear to swear a great oath to me, goddess, not to plot any more evil that is meant to do me harm.
sentences.zh: 奥德修斯说：“绝不，除非你发誓不再对我施加任何恶毒的计谋，女神。”

sentences.en: And Circe swears the oath and then Odysseus goes to bed with her.
sentences.zh: 喀耳刻发了誓，于是奥德修斯与她同床共枕。

sentences.en: She then restores his men to human form younger than before, far more handsome now and much taller to look upon.
sentences.zh: 随后，她将他的手下恢复了人形，他们变得比以前更年轻、更英俊、更高大。

sentences.en: So that's all worked out well.
sentences.zh: 所以一切都圆满解决了。

sentences.en: But then the twist, you might expect Odysseus to rush off, you know, but he doesn't.
sentences.zh: 但随后出现了转折，你可能以为奥德修斯会急着离开，但他没有。

sentences.en: He stays for a year.
sentences.zh: 他待了一年。

sentences.en: He and his crew stay with Circe for a year, don't they?
sentences.zh: 他和他的船员在喀耳刻那里待了一年，不是吗？

sentences.en: And actually, Odysseus seems to be enjoying this so much that it's his men who come to him and say, have you forgotten about going home?
sentences.zh: 事实上，奥德修斯似乎乐在其中，以至于他的手下不得不来找他说：“你忘了我们要回家了吗？”

sentences.en: We were meant to be going home.
sentences.zh: 我们本该回家的。

sentences.en: Your house with its high built roof and the land of your father's is still is waiting for you, Ithaca.
sentences.zh: 你那屋顶高耸的家宅和父亲的土地还在等你，伊萨卡。

sentences.en: And come on, let's crack on and leave.
sentences.zh: 来吧，我们赶紧出发离开这里。

sentences.en: And what is going on here, do you think?
sentences.zh: 你觉得这到底是怎么回事？

sentences.en: So is this an allegory for sexual desire?
sentences.zh: 这是否是对性欲的寓言？

sentences.en: Is it female wiles?
sentences.zh: 这是女性的诱惑吗？

sentences.en: What's what's all this about?
sentences.zh: 这一切到底意味着什么？

sentences.en: It clearly complicates the notion of Odysseus as a man driven by a kind of, you know, an absolute focus on getting back to Ithaca and to his beloved wife, Penelope.
sentences.zh: 这显然让奥德修斯作为一个一心只想回到伊萨卡、回到他挚爱的妻子佩涅洛佩身边的男人形象变得复杂了。

sentences.en: And just, you know, people will obviously be wondering about this.
sentences.zh: 人们显然会对此感到好奇。

sentences.en: Odysseus is meant to be devoted to his wife.
sentences.zh: 奥德修斯本应忠于他的妻子。

sentences.en: His sexual relationship with Circe is a complete non-issue to Homer.
sentences.zh: 但在荷马看来，他与喀耳刻的性关系根本不是个问题。

sentences.en: It's expected that a man, no matter how much he may be devoted to his wife, will obviously sleep around him.
sentences.zh: 人们认为，一个男人无论多么忠于妻子，显然都会在外面寻花问柳。

sentences.en: It's an absolute given.
sentences.zh: 这是绝对默认的。

sentences.en: I think there is a kind of eeriness to this episode, though.
sentences.zh: 但我认为这一集有一种诡异感。

sentences.en: Obviously, it's not naturalistic because it's a woman who's turning people into pigs.
sentences.zh: 显然，这不符合自然规律，因为是一个女人把人变成了猪。

sentences.en: But I don't think we should understand the passage of time here as simply being, you know, he's having a great time.
sentences.zh: 但我不认为我们应该把这段时间的流逝仅仅理解为他过得很开心。

sentences.en: He fails to notice what's going on.
sentences.zh: 他没注意到发生了什么。

sentences.en: And then before you know it, a year's gone by.
sentences.zh: 还没回过神来，一年就过去了。

sentences.en: I think that there's a kind of quality of the shaman about Circe,
sentences.zh: 我认为喀耳刻身上有一种萨满的特质，

sentences.en: the sense that she has conducted Odysseus and his men into a dimension of mystery and magic where time moves at a different pace.
sentences.zh: 那种感觉是她将奥德修斯和他的手下带入了一个充满神秘和魔法的维度，在那里时间以不同的速度流逝。

sentences.en: And so what she's offering Odysseus, I think, is a kind of akin to an initiation.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为她提供给奥德修斯的，是一种类似于启蒙的东西。

sentences.en: And the year passes pretty much in the blink of an eye.
sentences.zh: 这一年几乎在眨眼间就过去了。

sentences.en: And when Odysseus goes through and says, I really want to carry on, Circe doesn't object to this.
sentences.zh: 当奥德修斯走过去说“我真的想继续前行”时，喀耳刻并没有反对。

sentences.en: But she says, before you do this, you must go even further beyond my island to the dwelling place of Hades and dread Persephone.
sentences.zh: 但她说：“在你这样做之前，你必须走得更远，越过我的岛屿，去往冥王哈得斯和可怕的珀耳塞福涅的居所。”

sentences.en: And Hades and Persephone are the king and queen of the dead.
sentences.zh: 哈得斯和珀耳塞福涅是死者的国王和王后。

sentences.en: They rule the underworld.
sentences.zh: 他们统治着冥界。

sentences.en: And Circe is sending Odysseus on to the land of Hades because here in the land of the dead, you've got mist, you've got cloud, it shrouds the farthest boundaries of ocean.
sentences.zh: 喀耳刻把奥德修斯送往哈得斯的领地，因为在那里，在死者的国度，有迷雾，有云层，笼罩着海洋最遥远的边界。

sentences.en: If he gets to the land of the dead, he can consult with someone who will be able to tell him the best way to get back home.
sentences.zh: 如果他能到达死者的国度，他就能咨询某个人，那个人能告诉他回家的最佳途径。

sentences.en: And this is the great prophet Teresias.
sentences.zh: 这就是伟大的先知提瑞西阿斯。

sentences.en: And we have already met him in an episode of The Rest is History, the episode that we did on Oedipus.
sentences.zh: 我们已经在《历史的余味》关于俄狄浦斯的那一集中见过他了。

sentences.en: And he's died and he's now in the underworld.
sentences.zh: 他已经死了，现在在冥界。

sentences.en: And I think there is something.
sentences.zh: 我觉得这有点意思。

sentences.en: It's a kind of something of the superhero franchise, isn't there, here?
sentences.zh: 这难道不有点像超级英雄系列电影吗？

sentences.en: That characters who are the star of one film kind of reappear as a bit of a bit part in another.
sentences.zh: 在一部电影中担任主角的角色，在另一部电影中又以配角身份出现。

sentences.en: Yeah, this is the Circe Cinematic Universe.
sentences.zh: 没错，这就是“喀耳刻电影宇宙”。

sentences.en: Actually, have you read Madeleine Miller's novel about Circe?
sentences.zh: 对了，你读过玛德琳·米勒关于喀耳刻的小说吗？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 读过。

sentences.en: Brilliant, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 很精彩，不是吗？

sentences.en: It gives you the whole episode from her perspective.
sentences.zh: 它从她的视角讲述了整个故事。

sentences.en: Anyway, Odysseus and Co, they go off to the land of Hades.
sentences.zh: 总之，奥德修斯一行人前往哈得斯的领地。

sentences.en: And this is something that nobody's ever done before.
sentences.zh: 这是以前从未有人做过的事情。

sentences.en: They're the first ship ever to sail to.
sentences.zh: 他们是第一艘航行到那里的船。

sentences.en: I mean, who knew that you could sail there?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，谁知道还能航行到那里呢？

sentences.en: This was a surprise to me.
sentences.zh: 这让我感到惊讶。

sentences.en: This is why you need Circe to tell you such things.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么你需要喀耳刻来告诉你这些事情。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: No one had ever thought to do it before.
sentences.zh: 以前没人想过要这么做。

sentences.en: And also Circe has told him what to do when he lands on the land of the dead.
sentences.zh: 而且喀耳刻也告诉了他登陆死者国度后该怎么做。

sentences.en: How to get the ghost to talk to him.
sentences.zh: 如何让鬼魂与他交谈。

sentences.en: Because there is a complication.
sentences.zh: 因为有一个难题。

sentences.en: Once you are a ghost, your ability to speak fades very rapidly until you have drunk blood.
sentences.zh: 一旦你成了鬼魂，你的说话能力会迅速衰退，直到你喝了血。

sentences.en: And so Circe has said, take a load of sheep, dig a trench.
sentences.zh: 所以喀耳刻说，带上一群羊，挖一条沟。

sentences.en: Then when you've dug the trench, slit the throats of the sheep and fill the trench with blood.
sentences.zh: 挖好沟后，割开羊的喉咙，让血填满沟槽。

sentences.en: The ghosts will be drawn by it like vampires.
sentences.zh: 鬼魂会被它吸引，就像吸血鬼一样。

sentences.en: And you have to keep the dead at bay until Tiresias has drunk.
sentences.zh: 你必须挡住死者，直到提瑞西阿斯喝下血。

sentences.en: And this is what Odysseus does.
sentences.zh: 这就是奥德修斯所做的。

sentences.en: Tiresias drinks the blood and then is able to talk.
sentences.zh: 提瑞西阿斯喝下血后，就能开口说话了。

sentences.en: And he gives Odysseus all kinds of brilliant travel tips.
sentences.zh: 他给了奥德修斯各种绝妙的旅行建议。

sentences.en: So he says, this is the crucial thing you have to bear in mind.
sentences.zh: 他说，这是你必须牢记的关键点。

sentences.en: You may find yourself landing on an island called Thrinacea.
sentences.zh: 你可能会发现自己登陆了一个叫特里纳基亚的岛屿。

sentences.en: And this island is sacred to Helios, the sun god Hyperion.
sentences.zh: 这座岛是太阳神赫利俄斯·许珀里翁的神圣之地。

sentences.en: This is the god mentioned in the opening that you read, Dominic.
sentences.zh: 这就是多米尼克你读到的开头中提到的神。

sentences.en: If you find yourself on this island, no matter what you do, do not kill and barbecue the cattle.
sentences.zh: 如果你发现自己在这个岛上，无论如何，千万不要杀死并烧烤那些牛。

sentences.en: You have the vibe of people who love nothing more than a barbecue.
sentences.zh: 你们给人的感觉就是一群除了烧烤什么都不爱的人。

sentences.en: He's absolutely kind of, you know, he's put his finger on them.
sentences.zh: 他绝对是，你知道的，他一眼就看穿了他们。

sentences.en: Yeah, Australians.
sentences.zh: 没错，澳大利亚人。

sentences.en: Don't have a barbecue.
sentences.zh: 别搞烧烤。

sentences.en: Just don't do it.
sentences.zh: 千万别做。

sentences.en: Because if you do, everything will go wrong.
sentences.zh: 因为如果你做了，一切都会出错。

sentences.en: And Tiresias tells Odysseus the details of what will go wrong.
sentences.zh: 提瑞西阿斯告诉了奥德修斯事情会如何出错的细节。

sentences.en: You will get back home late and hapless after losing all your comrades on a ship that is not your own.
sentences.zh: 你会迟到且不幸地回到家，在那之前，你所有的同伴都会在别人的船上丧生。

sentences.en: And of course, that is echoing the curse that Polyphemus had laid on Odysseus earlier.
sentences.zh: 当然，这呼应了波吕斐摩斯早先对奥德修斯下的诅咒。

sentences.en: And Tiresias goes on and says that if you and your men kill this cattle, you will find your halls when you get back home filled with braggarts.
sentences.zh: 提瑞西阿斯继续说，如果你和你的手下杀了这些牛，当你回到家时，你会发现你的大厅里挤满了狂妄之徒。

sentences.en: Pestering and courting your wife.
sentences.zh: 纠缠并追求你的妻子。

sentences.en: So just, you know, just don't go there.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道的，千万别去碰那些牛。

sentences.en: So Tiresias, you know, he's drunk his fill and then he gives this advice and then he kind of flits away in a kind of spectral manner.
sentences.zh: 提瑞西阿斯喝足了血，给出了建议，然后就像幽灵一样飘走了。

sentences.en: And then all the other shades start to feed on the blood.
sentences.zh: 接着，所有其他的阴魂都开始争食鲜血。

sentences.en: And I think, you know, an incredibly sinister scene.
sentences.zh: 我认为这是一个极其阴森的场景。

sentences.en: And then Odysseus talks to some of them.
sentences.zh: 然后奥德修斯与其中一些人交谈。

sentences.en: And among them is his mother who had died while he was away in Troy.
sentences.zh: 其中包括他的母亲，她在奥德修斯远征特洛伊期间去世了。

sentences.en: You know, he hadn't realized that she was dead.
sentences.zh: 他之前并不知道她已经去世了。

sentences.en: And three times he tries to embrace her.
sentences.zh: 他三次试图拥抱她。

sentences.en: And three times she just kind of melts in his arms like a shadow or a dream.
sentences.zh: 但三次她都像影子或梦境一样在他怀中消散了。

sentences.en: He meets Agamemnon, the king of men, the commander of the Achaeans at Troy.
sentences.zh: 他遇见了阿伽门农，万王之王，特洛伊战争中阿凯亚人的统帅。

sentences.en: He's been murdered by his wife, Clytemnestra.
sentences.zh: 他被他的妻子克吕泰涅斯特拉谋杀了。

sentences.en: And so he tells Odysseus the story of that.
sentences.zh: 于是他向奥德修斯讲述了那段往事。

sentences.en: And then very famously, Odysseus meets the great hero of the Iliad, the greatest of all the Achaean warriors, Achilles, the man who at the end of the Iliad had killed Hector,
sentences.zh: 然后，非常著名的是，奥德修斯遇见了《伊利亚特》中的伟大英雄，所有阿凯亚战士中最伟大的一位——阿喀琉斯，那个在《伊利亚特》结尾杀死了赫克托耳的人，

sentences.en: the greatest of the Trojan warriors.
sentences.zh: 赫克托耳是特洛伊最伟大的战士。

sentences.en: And Achilles had been offered the choice when he was very young of a life short, but full of glory or a long life, but living in obscurity.
sentences.zh: 阿喀琉斯在很年轻时就被给予了选择：是过短暂但充满荣耀的一生，还是过漫长但默默无闻的一生。

sentences.en: And Achilles tells Odysseus, I made a terrible mistake.
sentences.zh: 阿喀琉斯告诉奥德修斯：“我犯了一个可怕的错误。”

sentences.en: I went for the short life full of glory, but I would far rather live off the earth as the surf of another man,
sentences.zh: “我选择了充满荣耀的短暂一生，但我宁愿在世间做一个为他人耕作的雇工。”

sentences.en: some man with a pitiful portion who barely ekes out a living than rule here as the Lord of all those who are dead and gone.
sentences.zh: 比起在这里统治所有死者，做一个勉强糊口、生活困顿的凡人要好得多。

sentences.en: So to me, that is the single most interesting moment of the entire Odyssey,
sentences.zh: 所以对我来说，这是《奥德赛》全篇中最耐人寻味的一个时刻，

sentences.en: because it undermines the cult of the hero and the sort of the emphasis on glory and martial vigor and writing your name in neon letters that will never fade and all of that kind of thing.
sentences.zh: 因为它动摇了英雄崇拜，也动摇了那种对荣耀、尚武精神、以及将自己的名字刻在永不褪色的霓虹灯上这类事物的推崇。

sentences.en: And basically, Homer is implying that there is an argument for saying, it's a bit like in the Madeleine Miller book, Circe, this is what Telemachus says, it's better to be obscure.
sentences.zh: 基本上，荷马是在暗示一种观点，这有点像玛德琳·米勒在《喀耳刻》一书中所写的那样，这也是忒勒马科斯所说的：默默无闻其实更好。

sentences.en: It's actually better to have a nice, quiet life and no one knows you even exist than to be a great hero and, you know,
sentences.zh: 过上平静安稳的生活，没人知道你的存在，其实比做一个伟大的英雄要好得多，而且你知道，

sentences.en: to be wreathed in glory and stuff that that is all that that all passes and it's meaningless.
sentences.zh: 被荣耀光环笼罩什么的，那一切终将逝去，毫无意义。

sentences.en: Yes, that I think that's absolutely what he's saying.
sentences.zh: 是的，我想这绝对就是他想表达的意思。

sentences.en: But also what is what Achilles is saying essentially is the greatest of all gifts is immortality.
sentences.zh: 但阿喀琉斯本质上也在说，所有馈赠中最伟大的就是永生。

sentences.en: You know, you never want to die.
sentences.zh: 你知道，你永远都不想死。

sentences.en: If you ever get offered the gift of immortality, you want to embrace it with open arMs.
sentences.zh: 如果有人给你永生的馈赠，你一定会张开双臂去拥抱它。

sentences.en: I mean, that is essentially what he's saying and that is something that will impact on a decision that Odysseus has to make in due course, but we will come to that.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这本质上就是他所说的，而这一点也会影响奥德修斯在适当时候必须做出的决定，但我们稍后再谈。

sentences.en: But do you think Homer genuinely means it that his listeners should have a think about their cult of glory and all of that or not?
sentences.zh: 但你认为荷马是真心希望他的听众去反思他们对荣耀的崇拜以及诸如此类的事情吗？

sentences.en: I think that it is one of the things that shadows the Greek devotion to competition, to heroism, to courage,
sentences.zh: 我认为，希腊人对竞争、英雄主义、勇气和荣耀的推崇，其背后笼罩着一层阴影，

sentences.en: to glory is the fact that there is no equivalent of the Christian or Muslim heaven for all but the very greateSt.
sentences.zh: 那就是除了极少数伟大人物外，并没有一个等同于基督教或伊斯兰教天堂的地方。

sentences.en: That death is a shadowy, dull existence where you're a kind of a gibbering shadow who has to drink blood even to speak.
sentences.zh: 死亡是一种阴暗、沉闷的存在，你变成了一个只会吱吱乱叫的影子，甚至必须喝血才能开口说话。

sentences.en: I mean, it's, you know, there's nothing there.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你知道，那里什么都没有。

sentences.en: And so it makes the blaze of life all the more kind of glorious.
sentences.zh: 所以这反而让生命之火显得更加辉煌灿烂。

sentences.en: So anyway, as you say, I mean, it is an amazing, amazing moment in the poem and in the kind of broader sweep of ancient Greek culture.
sentences.zh: 总之，正如你所说，这确实是史诗中，乃至整个古希腊文化长河中一个令人惊叹的时刻。

sentences.en: So Odysseus has got what he came for.
sentences.zh: 奥德修斯得到了他想要的东西。

sentences.en: He's got this advice from Tiresias.
sentences.zh: 他从特瑞西阿斯那里得到了建议。

sentences.en: And so now he goes back to the Lady Circe who feasts them.
sentences.zh: 于是他回到喀耳刻女神那里，女神款待了他们。

sentences.en: And then after the meal, she says to Odysseus, OK, just go.
sentences.zh: 用餐后，她对奥德修斯说，好了，走吧。

sentences.en: As soon as dawn appears, set sail.
sentences.zh: 黎明一出现，就扬帆起航。

sentences.en: And she then advises him on how he should negotiate the various dangers that will be awaiting him on the next stage of his voyage.
sentences.zh: 随后她建议他如何应对在下一段航程中等待他的各种危险。

sentences.en: And she says, you are going to be passing the island of the sirens.
sentences.zh: 她说，你们将会经过塞壬女妖居住的岛屿。

sentences.en: And these are carnivorous creatures, heads of women, bodies of birds.
sentences.zh: 这些是食肉生物，长着女人的头，鸟的身体。

sentences.en: They have irresistibly beautiful voices.
sentences.zh: 她们拥有令人无法抗拒的美妙歌声。

sentences.en: So that's what the word siren means.
sentences.zh: 这就是“塞壬”这个词的含义。

sentences.en: And they sit on this island perched amid a great pile of bones.
sentences.zh: 她们坐在岛上，栖息在一堆巨大的白骨之中。

sentences.en: And Circe has a suggestion.
sentences.zh: 喀耳刻有个建议。

sentences.en: She says, all your men should put wax in their ears so they can't hear it.
sentences.zh: 她说，你们所有人都要用蜡封住耳朵，这样就听不到歌声了。

sentences.en: And you, if you want to hear the song of the sirens, get your men to tie you to the mast and you will hear the song.
sentences.zh: 而你，如果你想听塞壬的歌声，就让手下把你绑在桅杆上，这样你就能听到歌声。

sentences.en: You will order them to set you free.
sentences.zh: 你会命令他们放开你。

sentences.en: Tell them on no account to set you free.
sentences.zh: 告诉他们无论如何都不要放开你。

sentences.en: And that way you can hear the song of the sirens and live to tell the tale.
sentences.zh: 这样你既能听到塞壬的歌声，又能活着讲出这段经历。

sentences.en: And then after that, you will pass two terrible monsters, Scylla and Charybdis.
sentences.zh: 在那之后，你们会经过两个可怕的怪物：斯库拉和卡律布狄斯。

sentences.en: And these guard the passage between two cliffs and you have to sail between them.
sentences.zh: 它们守卫着两座悬崖之间的通道，你们必须从中间穿过。

sentences.en: And in one of these cliffs, and this is a cliff which reaches all the way up to wide heaven and is ringed by a cloud of dark blue.
sentences.zh: 在其中一座悬崖上——这是一座直插云霄、被深蓝色云雾环绕的悬崖——

sentences.en: There is a cave.
sentences.zh: 有一个洞穴。

sentences.en: And inside this cave lurks the monster Scylla.
sentences.zh: 洞穴里潜伏着怪物斯库拉。

sentences.en: And Scylla makes a noise like a little newborn puppy.
sentences.zh: 斯库拉发出的声音像刚出生的小狗一样。

sentences.en: So it's so very, very sweet.
sentences.zh: 所以听起来非常、非常可爱。

sentences.en: However, Scylla has six necks, enormously long.
sentences.zh: 然而，斯库拉有六个脖子，长得惊人。

sentences.en: And on top of each of the necks is a head harrowing sight, each with three rows of teeth.
sentences.zh: 每个脖子上都长着一个令人毛骨悚然的头，每张嘴里都有三排牙齿。

sentences.en: So not good news.
sentences.zh: 所以这不是什么好消息。

sentences.en: A bit like the alien in the Scorny Weaver film.
sentences.zh: 有点像西格妮·韦弗电影里的异形。

sentences.en: And from the other cliff sprouts a huge wild fig tree.
sentences.zh: 另一座悬崖上长着一棵巨大的野无花果树。

sentences.en: And beneath that, in the depths of the waters, lurks Charybdis.
sentences.zh: 在它下方，深水之中，潜伏着卡律布狄斯。

sentences.en: This is the second monster.
sentences.zh: 这是第二个怪物。

sentences.en: And every day, Charybdis sucks the water down.
sentences.zh: 每天，卡律布狄斯都会把海水吸下去。

sentences.en: And then thrice each day, she vomits it up.
sentences.zh: 然后每天三次，她又会把水吐出来。

sentences.en: Thrice, she gulps it back down.
sentences.zh: 三次，她又把它吞回去。

sentences.en: And this creates a monstrous whirlpool.
sentences.zh: 这会形成一个巨大的漩涡。

sentences.en: And any ship that gets caught in the whirlpool is doomed.
sentences.zh: 任何被卷入漩涡的船只都难逃一劫。

sentences.en: It will be dragged round and round, down and down into the jaws of Charybdis.
sentences.zh: 它会被拖得团团转，一直沉入卡律布狄斯的血盆大口中。

sentences.en: And everyone on that ship will be eaten.
sentences.zh: 船上的每个人都会被吃掉。

sentences.en: And so Scylla's advice is steer clear of the whirlpool.
sentences.zh: 所以斯库拉的建议是：避开漩涡。

sentences.en: Stick close to Scylla's rock.
sentences.zh: 紧贴着斯库拉的岩石航行。

sentences.en: For as Scylla says, it is better by far to mourn six of the men from your ship than to mourn all of them together.
sentences.zh: 因为正如斯库拉所说，哀悼船上的六个人，远比哀悼所有人要好得多。

sentences.en: And as for the cattle of the sun, which Tiresias had been majoring on, Scylla says, look, just don't land there.
sentences.zh: 至于特瑞西阿斯重点提到的太阳神的牛群，斯库拉说，听着，千万别在那儿登陆。

sentences.en: It's too dangerous.
sentences.zh: 太危险了。

sentences.en: She's obviously sussed out the enthusiasm of Odysseus' men for barbecues and says, just, you know, don't let them have the temptation.
sentences.zh: 她显然看穿了奥德修斯手下对烧烤的热衷，所以说，你知道，别让他们受到诱惑。

sentences.en: So Odysseus has got this advice from Scylla.
sentences.zh: 奥德修斯得到了斯库拉的这些建议。

sentences.en: He follows it to the letter.
sentences.zh: 他严格地执行了。

sentences.en: He does indeed become the only man to have heard the siren sing and live to tell the tale.
sentences.zh: 他确实成了唯一一个听过塞壬歌唱并活着讲出这段经历的人。

sentences.en: He does lose six men to the six sneaking necks of Scylla that kind of descend from her cave and grabs them and kind of pulls them up into her cave and devours them.
sentences.zh: 他确实损失了六个人，被斯库拉那六个从洞穴中伸出的脖子抓走，拖进洞穴吞食了。

sentences.en: But they manage to avoid the whirlpool of Charybdis.
sentences.zh: 但他们成功避开了卡律布狄斯的漩涡。

sentences.en: And that's the main thing.
sentences.zh: 这才是最重要的。

sentences.en: And they sail on and they see the island of the sun.
sentences.zh: 他们继续航行，看到了太阳神的岛屿。

sentences.en: And Odysseus says, OK, we're not stopping here.
sentences.zh: 奥德修斯说，好了，我们不能在这里停留。

sentences.en: No way.
sentences.zh: 绝对不行。

sentences.en: Because this is the bit, remember, Tiresias, you're better to avoid it.
sentences.zh: 因为记得吗，特瑞西阿斯说过，最好避开这里。

sentences.en: Do not touch them.
sentences.zh: 千万别碰它们。

sentences.en: Of course, as soon as Tiresias said that, surely we all knew what was going to happen.
sentences.zh: 当然，特瑞西阿斯一说这话，我们肯定都知道会发生什么了。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Odysseus' men, when he says, look, we're not stopping here.
sentences.zh: 当奥德修斯说，听着，我们不能在这里停留时，

sentences.en: They all complain.
sentences.zh: 他们全都抱怨起来。

sentences.en: They say, look, oh, God, we're shattered.
sentences.zh: 他们说，天哪，我们累垮了。

sentences.en: You know, we really need a break.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我们真的需要休息一下。

sentences.en: It looks really nice.
sentences.zh: 这里看起来真不错。

sentences.en: Please come on.
sentences.zh: 求你了，拜托。

sentences.en: So very reluctantly, Odysseus says, OK, but guys, whatever you do, don't touch the cattle.
sentences.zh: 所以奥德修斯非常不情愿地说，好吧，但伙计们，无论你们做什么，千万别碰那些牛。

sentences.en: You know, just don't go there.
sentences.zh: 你知道，千万别去动它们。

sentences.en: We will stop there for a single afternoon and then we will continue on our way.
sentences.zh: 我们只在这里停留一个下午，然后就继续赶路。

sentences.en: So they land.
sentences.zh: 于是他们登陆了。

sentences.en: And so they're stuck there and they're really, really hungry.
sentences.zh: 他们被困在那里，而且真的非常非常饿。

sentences.en: Their supplies are running out.
sentences.zh: 补给快用完了。

sentences.en: And Odysseus can see his men starting to eye up the cattle and thinking how nice, you know, chunks of this cattle would be if it were on a spit, you know, in a lovely kebab.
sentences.zh: 奥德修斯能看出手下开始盯着那些牛，心想如果把这些牛烤成肉串，做成美味的烤肉，该有多好。

sentences.en: And so in desperation, he thinks, well, listen, clearly there is a God here who's angry.
sentences.zh: 于是他绝望地想，好吧，听着，显然这里有位神灵在发怒。

sentences.en: I need to get up onto the top of the mountain at the center of this island and raise a prayer there.
sentences.zh: 我得爬到岛中心那座山的山顶去祈祷。

sentences.en: So that's what he does.
sentences.zh: 于是他照做了。

sentences.en: And he leaves his men behind and he heads off to the summit of the mountain on the top in the middle of the island to raise prayers to the gods.
sentences.zh: 他把手下留在后面，独自前往岛中央的山顶，向众神祈祷。

sentences.en: And presumably before he goes, he does remind them, guys, don't eat the cattle.
sentences.zh: 想必在他离开之前，他肯定提醒过他们：伙计们，别吃那些牛。

sentences.en: Don't eat the cattle.
sentences.zh: 别吃那些牛。

sentences.en: Did I mention don't eat the cattle?
sentences.zh: 我提到过别吃那些牛吗？

sentences.en: He reaches the mountain top as before with the winds of Iolus in the bag.
sentences.zh: 他到达了山顶，就像之前带着埃俄罗斯的风袋时一样。

sentences.en: So now, faithfully, he falls asleep.
sentences.zh: 于是现在，他放心地睡着了。

sentences.en: So there's something of the Lafayette about Odysseus falling asleep at crucial moments.
sentences.zh: 奥德修斯在关键时刻睡着，这倒有点像拉法耶特侯爵的作风。

sentences.en: And as he sleeps, his men obviously do what they've been told not to do.
sentences.zh: 在他睡觉的时候，他的手下显然做了他们被禁止做的事。

sentences.en: They kill and roast the sacred cattle and the smell of kebabs drifts into the nostrils of Odysseus.
sentences.zh: 他们杀死了神圣的牛并进行烧烤，烤肉的香味飘进了奥德修斯的鼻子里。

sentences.en: He wakes up, he looks down, he sees the smoke's rising.
sentences.zh: 他醒来，向下望去，看到烟雾升起。

sentences.en: He goes, oh, no.
sentences.zh: 他心想，噢，不。

sentences.en: And he runs down and for six days, his men make a feaSt.
sentences.zh: 他跑下山去，他的手下已经狂欢了六天。

sentences.en: The wind, you know, they can't leave because of the winds.
sentences.zh: 风，你知道，因为风的原因他们无法离开。

sentences.en: But it is very obvious that nothing good is going to come of this barbecue because the skins of the slain cattle keep moving around and the meat on the kebab sticks keeps lowing.
sentences.zh: 但很明显，这场烧烤不会有什么好结果，因为被杀的牛皮在不停地移动，烤肉串上的肉也在不停地哞哞叫。

sentences.en: That's like a vegan's fantasy, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 那简直是素食者的噩梦，不是吗？

sentences.en: Like, yeah.
sentences.zh: 就像是，没错。

sentences.en: And it's not surprising because it is, I think, hard to overemphasize the scale of the insult that has been done to the sun god because these are clearly solar cattle.
sentences.zh: 这并不奇怪，因为我认为，无论怎么强调对太阳神造成的侮辱程度都不为过，因为这些显然是太阳神的牛。

sentences.en: And notions of solar cattle seem to have been very widespread in the myths of the ancient Indo-Europeans.
sentences.zh: 太阳牛的概念似乎在古代印欧人的神话中非常普遍。

sentences.en: So the Greeks are Indo-Europeans.
sentences.zh: 所以希腊人也是印欧人。

sentences.en: You get it in Hindi mythology and Irish mythology from India to Ireland, in other words.
sentences.zh: 你在印度神话和爱尔兰神话中都能看到，换句话说，从印度到爱尔兰都有。

sentences.en: And their theft in all these stories, no matter where they're told, it always represents a kind of massive insult to the cosmic order.
sentences.zh: 在所有这些故事中，无论在哪里讲述，偷窃这些牛总是代表着对宇宙秩序的一种巨大亵渎。

sentences.en: And so it is in the Odyssey.
sentences.zh: 在《奥德赛》中也是如此。

sentences.en: Helios, the sun god, complains to Zeus.
sentences.zh: 太阳神赫利俄斯向宙斯告状。

sentences.en: Zeus stills the storMs.
sentences.zh: 宙斯平息了风暴。

sentences.en: So there's a very sinister calm.
sentences.zh: 所以出现了一种非常阴森的平静。

sentences.en: And this allows Odysseus and his men to set sail.
sentences.zh: 这让奥德修斯和他的手下得以扬帆起航。

sentences.en: And then all at once, once the ship is out at sea,
sentences.zh: 然后就在那一瞬间，当船驶入公海时，

sentences.en: Zeus thundered and hurled his lightning at the ship.
sentences.zh: 宙斯发出雷鸣，向船投下了闪电。

sentences.en: And the mast of the ship snaps.
sentences.zh: 船的桅杆断裂了。

sentences.en: And as it falls, it brains the helmsman and knocks him into the sea.
sentences.zh: 桅杆倒下时，砸碎了舵手的脑袋，把他撞进了海里。

sentences.en: So they now have no one to steer them.
sentences.zh: 所以他们现在没人掌舵了。

sentences.en: The ship spins round and round.
sentences.zh: 船只不停地打转。

sentences.en: The decking blazes with smoke like sulfur.
sentences.zh: 甲板上燃起硫磺味的烟雾。

sentences.en: And all of Odysseus' men are tossed into the kind of the great boiling royal of the sea, looking just like cormorants.
sentences.zh: 奥德修斯所有的手下都被抛进了波涛汹涌的大海中，看起来就像鸬鹚一样。

sentences.en: They bobbed about on the waves all around the black hull ship.
sentences.zh: 他们在黑色船壳周围的波浪中起伏。

sentences.en: The god snatched their homecoming from them.
sentences.zh: 神夺走了他们回家的路。

sentences.en: But only one man survives the shipwreck.
sentences.zh: 但只有一个人在海难中幸存下来。

sentences.en: And this is Odysseus himself.
sentences.zh: 那就是奥德修斯本人。

sentences.en: Somehow he manages to fashion a raft out of all the wreckage, all the flotsam and jetsam.
sentences.zh: 他不知怎的设法用所有的残骸、所有的漂浮物拼凑成了一只木筏。

sentences.en: But even now, even though he's got his raft, he's still not safe.
sentences.zh: 但即便如此，尽管他有了木筏，他依然不安全。

sentences.en: Because the wind changes and blows him back the way he had come towards Scylla and Charybdis.
sentences.zh: 因为风向改变，把他吹回了原路，朝斯库拉和卡律布狄斯的方向吹去。

sentences.en: And of course, he can't steer.
sentences.zh: 当然，他无法掌舵。

sentences.en: So the whirlpool is swirling downwards.
sentences.zh: 所以漩涡正在向下旋转。

sentences.en: Charybdis is sucking the water down deep into her jaws.
sentences.zh: 卡律布狄斯正把海水深深地吸进她的血盆大口中。

sentences.en: And Odysseus' raft gets caught up in the kind of the spinning and the whirling of the waters.
sentences.zh: 奥德修斯的木筏被卷入了水的旋转和漩涡之中。

sentences.en: As it's going down, Odysseus leaps up from the raft.
sentences.zh: 就在木筏下沉时，奥德修斯从木筏上跳了起来。

sentences.en: And he clings on to that giant fig tree, remember, which Homer had told us was leaning over the whirlpool.
sentences.zh: 他紧紧抓住那棵巨大的无花果树，记得吗，荷马告诉过我们它正悬在漩涡上方。

sentences.en: And he manages to hold on to it until the raft is spat back up by Charybdis.
sentences.zh: 他设法抓住了它，直到木筏被卡律布狄斯吐出来。

sentences.en: And he drops down from the branch that he's been holding on to down beside the timbers.
sentences.zh: 然后他从一直抓着的树枝上跳下来，落在了木材旁边。

sentences.en: And sitting on top of them, as he later describes it, I used my hands to paddle away.
sentences.zh: 他坐在木材上，正如他后来描述的那样，我用双手划水逃离了。

sentences.en: And for nine days and nine nights, he drifts.
sentences.zh: 他在海上漂流了九天九夜。

sentences.en: And he is the only man left alive out of what had originally been a fleet of 12 ships.
sentences.zh: 他是原本由12艘船组成的船队中唯一幸存的人。

sentences.en: And the loss of those men in Homer's poem is very deeply felt because the Odyssey throughout the account of its hero's voyages, and obviously the focus is very much on the hero.
sentences.zh: 在荷马的诗篇中，这些人的损失被刻画得非常深刻，因为《奥德赛》通篇都在讲述英雄的航行，显然焦点非常集中在英雄身上。

sentences.en: Nevertheless, it is unusual for the emphasis that it places on the minor characters.
sentences.zh: 尽管如此，它对次要角色的重视程度还是很不寻常的。

sentences.en: You kind of come to know them.
sentences.zh: 你渐渐地了解了他们。

sentences.en: We haven't really been talking about them much because we haven't had the time.
sentences.zh: 我们之前并没有怎么谈论他们，因为没有时间。

sentences.en: But when you're reading the poem, you feel for them.
sentences.zh: 但当你阅读这首诗时，你会为他们感到难过。

sentences.en: You mark their fates, even if they are idiots, with their enthusiasm for barbecues.
sentences.zh: 你记住了他们的命运，即使他们是一群热衷于烧烤的笨蛋。

sentences.en: I mean, they've only got themselves to blame, to be honeSt.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，老实说，他们只能怪自己。

sentences.en: And again, Scilla and Charybdis, all of this stuff, you can see how this reflects the anxieties of an Asian exploration and sea travel.
sentences.zh: 再说一次，斯库拉和卡律布狄斯，所有这些东西，你可以看出这反映了当时人们对亚洲探险和海上航行的焦虑。

sentences.en: The whirlpool, the cliffs, all of that.
sentences.zh: 漩涡、悬崖，所有这些。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So Scilla and Charybdis was identified with the Straits of Messina between Sicily and Italy,
sentences.zh: 所以斯库拉和卡律布狄斯被认为是西西里岛和意大利之间的墨西拿海峡，

sentences.en: where you have whirlpools and riptides, and it was generally dreaded by ancient sailors.
sentences.zh: 那里有漩涡和激流，古代水手通常对那里感到恐惧。

sentences.en: And through nature, the island of the cattle means three headlands.
sentences.zh: 从自然地理来看，牛之岛意味着三个岬角。

sentences.en: Sicily has three headlands.
sentences.zh: 西西里岛就有三个岬角。

sentences.en: So again, it was identified with Sicily.
sentences.zh: 所以再次说明，它被认定为西西里岛。

sentences.en: And Sicily was the kind of main focus for Greek colonization in this period.
sentences.zh: 而西西里岛是这一时期希腊殖民的主要焦点。

sentences.en: So it's perhaps not surprising that it generated all these kind of, all these myths.
sentences.zh: 所以它产生了所有这些神话，或许并不令人惊讶。

sentences.en: But now, with the loss of his men and his ship, Odysseus, I think, is drifting back from the kind of the shipping lanes
sentences.zh: 但现在，随着船员和船只的损失，我认为奥德修斯正从希腊水手可能熟悉的航道上漂流开来，

sentences.en: that Greek sailors might recognize, back into a dimension beyond the mortal, back through the kind of the Homeric equivalent of a wormhole.
sentences.zh: 回到了凡人维度之外，回到了荷马史诗中类似虫洞的地方。

sentences.en: And it's telling, I think, that Homer does not describe in detail what happens next.
sentences.zh: 我认为很有意思的是，荷马并没有详细描述接下来发生了什么。

sentences.en: All he really reports is that after nine days of drifting on the open seas, and this is Odysseus narrating at this point,
sentences.zh: 他真正记录的只是，在公海漂流了九天之后——此时是奥德修斯自己在叙述——

sentences.en: on the 9th of the 10th, I was brought by the gods to the island of Agigia, home of Calypso, she of the beautiful braids, dread goddess who speaks like a mortal.
sentences.zh: 第十天的第九天，我被神带到了奥吉吉亚岛，那是拥有美丽发辫的卡吕普索的家，她是一位像凡人一样说话的可怕女神。

sentences.en: She welcomed and cared for me.
sentences.zh: 她欢迎并照顾了我。

sentences.en: So it's slightly Circe-like, but the difference here is that whereas he stayed with Circe voluntarily,
sentences.zh: 所以这有点像喀耳刻，但不同之处在于，他当初是自愿留在喀耳刻那里的，

sentences.en: Calypso will not let him leave.
sentences.zh: 而卡吕普索却不让他离开。

sentences.en: That's right, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 是这样吧，对吗？

sentences.en: He's staying here almost against his will, day after day, month after month, year after year.
sentences.zh: 他几乎是违心地留在这里，日复一日，月复一月，年复一年。

sentences.en: He is, you know, weeping.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他在哭泣。

sentences.en: He's thinking about Penelope.
sentences.zh: 他在想念佩涅洛佩。

sentences.en: He's thinking about his son Telemachus, about Ithaca, his home.
sentences.zh: 他在想念他的儿子特勒马科斯，想念他的家乡伊萨卡。

sentences.en: And the greatest punishment of all, every night he has to go to bed with Calypso.
sentences.zh: 而最痛苦的惩罚是，他每天晚上都必须和卡吕普索同床共枕。

sentences.en: What a terrible ordeal this must have been.
sentences.zh: 这一定是一场多么可怕的折磨啊。

sentences.en: Yes, to quote Homer, compelled by the goddess to do so, he unwilling, she all too willing.
sentences.zh: 是的，引用荷马的话，他是在女神的强迫下才这么做的，他心不甘情不愿，而她却乐此不疲。

sentences.en: So basically, Dominic, he's become a beautiful goddess's sex slave to a terrible fate.
sentences.zh: 所以基本上，多米尼克，他已经沦为一位美丽女神的性奴，陷入了可怕的命运。

sentences.en: Oh no, what a terrible fate that is.
sentences.zh: 噢不，那真是太可怕的命运了。

sentences.en: So, wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: Will he ever escape, Tom?
sentences.zh: 他能逃脱吗，汤姆？

sentences.en: And if so, how will he do it?
sentences.zh: 如果能，他会怎么做？

sentences.en: And what will happen when he gets back to Ithaca?
sentences.zh: 当他回到伊萨卡时会发生什么？

sentences.en: If only there was some way I could find out the answers to all these questions, because I know you have amazing stories yet to tell us.
sentences.zh: 要是能有什么办法让我找到所有这些问题的答案就好了，因为我知道你还有精彩的故事要讲给我们听。

sentences.en: I do.
sentences.zh: 我确实有。

sentences.en: And brilliantly, Dominic, there is a way you can find out.
sentences.zh: 太棒了，多米尼克，确实有办法让你找到答案。

sentences.en: You can listen to the second episode of this literally epic.
sentences.zh: 你可以收听这个史诗系列的第二集。

sentences.en: I mean, literally epic, yeah.
sentences.zh: 我是说，真正的史诗，没错。

sentences.en: And if you would like to get early access, and you're not already a member of the Rest is History Club,
